job.title: Partner, Executive Search
job.description:
Partner, Executive Search

You've built your reputation. Now build your legacy.

You've already built a successful executive search career. The question now is: what do you want to build next?

Perhaps it's a stronger market presence. Deeper client relationships. A practice that's recognised for trusted advice. Or perhaps it's the opportunity to help shape a business, not just work in one.

If that's where you are, we'd like to talk.

Why now?

Leadership has never mattered more. Organisations are making long-term decisions about the people who will lead through growth, change and uncertainty. As we continue to invest in our executive search capability, we're looking for a Partner who wants to help shape what comes next.

This isn't about inheriting someone else's portfolio. It's about building your own.

Imagine 12 months from now

You're a trusted adviser to CEOs, boards and executive leaders.

You've built a portfolio of retained executive search work that reflects your strengths, your relationships and your reputation.

You're working alongside experienced Partners who share opportunities, challenge your thinking and celebrate your success.

You're helping shape the future of Davidson Executive & Talent, influencing how we grow while supporting the next generation of consultants.

Most importantly, you've built something that's genuinely yours.

Why this is different

Most firms ask you to fit into an existing structure.

We're looking for someone to help shape ours.

At Davidson, you'll have the autonomy to build your own practice with the backing of a national business that brings together expertise across people, strategy and technology. Executive search often opens the door to broader conversations around leadership, capability and organisational performance. Our integrated model helps you build deeper client relationships and create greater impact.

Davidson brings together expertise across people, strategy and technology to help organisations perform at their best. Founded in 1991, we listen closely, understand the challenge and apply practical, experience-led thinking that helps organisations move forward with confidence. Our focus is on bringing clarity to complexity and supporting stronger, more resilient futures.

Within Davidson Executive & Talent, we partner with organisations to secure and support specialist talent, from early career professionals through to executive and board leaders.

Let's have a conversation.

If you're looking for the freedom to build your market, the support of experienced colleagues and the opportunity to shape what's next, we'd welcome a confidential conversation.


Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact peopleandculture@davidsonwp.com, quoting reference JN -102026-44470. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: Chief Member Experience Officer - Incolink
job.description:
• Lead Incolink’s end-to-end member experience strategy
  • Build a transparent, compliant and high-performing service model
  • Deliver lasting impact for workers, families and the construction industry

Incolink is Australia’s largest provider of severance benefits and income protection for workers in the commercial building and construction industry. Through its employer and union partnership, Incolink provides critical financial protection, health, wellbeing and practical support to members and their families. Incolink is a purpose-led, member-based organisation operating at the intersection of construction, financial services, insurance and worker wellbeing.

The organisation currently has a strong net approval rating and is continuing to strengthen its service model within an increasingly regulated environment. This includes building greater compliance maturity, clearer risk identification, stronger governance, improved claims administration, enhanced contact centre performance, greater service transparency and stronger organisational accountability.

The Opportunity

Incolink is seeking an experienced and purpose-led executive to lead its end-to-end member experience across the business. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and joining the Executive Leadership Team, the Chief Member Experience Officer will be the executive owner of Incolink’s member proposition and member experience. The role will connect member insight, service delivery, service standards, communications and the effective management of member-facing offerings. The Chief Member Experience Officer will shape a consistent, accessible and high-performing service model across different business units.

The successful candidate will improve how members experience Incolink across all service channels while ensuring that processes are transparent, consistent, compliant and aligned to member needs. The role will require a careful balance between innovation and control. The Chief Member Officer will improve service delivery and member engagement without compromising compliance, risk management, financial sustainability or Incolink’s important employer–union relationships.

Key Priorities

  • Establishing credibility quickly and assessing the current operating environment, service model and member experience.
  • Embedding a strong risk and compliance culture across the member-facing organisation.
  • Strengthening claims processing, contact center operations, service procedures and member resolution pathways. Also ensuring staff understand and consistently apply minimum regulatory, risk and service standards.
  • Improving member journeys, service transparency, accountability and operational consistency.
  • Introducing stronger service reporting and dashboards, including visibility of contact center performance, average handling times, service quality and member outcomes.
  • Reviewing the effectiveness and relevance of current member-facing services and offerings.
  • Using member insight, complaints, feedback and service data to identify opportunities for innovation and improvement.
  • Strengthening partner governance and performance across member-facing services. Whilst building the capability, confidence and accountability of employees across a multidisciplinary service environment.
  • Developing trusted relationships with union stakeholders while remaining neutral, credible and balanced across employer and employee interests.
  • Establishing clear interfaces with the CEO and other executives across operations, risk, compliance, communications and stakeholder engagement.
  • Supporting a culture of accountability, continuous improvement and high-quality service delivery.

This is a rare opportunity to shape the member experience strategy of a member-led organisation with a direct and lasting impact on Australia’s construction industry. You will influence how workers and employers access financial protection, health, wellbeing and practical support throughout their working lives, while helping strengthen the resilience of the broader industry.

With responsibility across member services, operations, health and wellbeing, industry engagement and partner-delivered services, the role offers the opportunity to create a more connected, accessible and contemporary member experience at scale. It is a highly visible executive leadership position for someone motivated by purpose, meaningful transformation and the opportunity to deliver measurable value to members, their families and industry stakeholders.

To view the Success Profile for this opportunity, please copy and paste the following link into your browser: https://tinyurl.com/mv4v5r92

To apply, please click ‘apply now’ and upload your CV and Cover Letter. For any questions not outlined in the PD and for a confidential discussion, please contact Anthony Grey at 0403 310 566 or Richard van Ark at 0412 831 614. Davidson acknowledges the Traditional Custodians of the lands on which we work and live. We are also committed to equal opportunity and strive to promote diversity, inclusion, belonging, flexibility, and accessibility in all that we do. Should you require assistance in your interactions with us or through a recruitment process, please let us know so we can provide adjustments for you.

Applications close on 23rd October 2026 5pm.

job.title: Control Centre Systems Engineer
job.description:
About the Company

Iberdrola Australia is leading Australia’s transition to a clean energy future. With over 125 years history, the Iberdrola Group today is a global energy leader. Their expertise includes renewable energy, networks, smart grids, large-scale energy storage, energy innovation and digitisation, and advanced customer products.

Their generation portfolio is more than 95% renewable and includes 10 wind farms, 3 solar farms, 4 grid scale batteries and 2 fast-start peakers and continuing to evolve, investing in new capabilities in networks and offshore wind. Iberdrola’s financial strength, supply chain access and history of award-winning expertise, will make Iberdrola a certain partner to accelerate Australia’s Net Zero emissions future.

Iberdrola is now recruiting for a Control Centre Systems Engineer to provide technical support to the Control Centre operations across wind, solar, gas and battery energy storage assets. The role is based in the Sydney CBD office.

This is an opportunity to shape your career with one of the genuine global energy leaders within Australia.


About the Role

Reporting to the General Manager, the Control Centre Systems Engineer will support, maintain and develop the operational technology and control centre systems that will enable the safe, secure and reliable operation of Iberdrola Australia renewable energy assets.

The role provides day-to-day technical support to Operations Control Centre (OCC) operations and contributes to system improvements, deployment projects and global standardisation initiatives. It also acts as a technical interface between Operations, Energy Markets, Engineering, IT, OT, Cybersecurity, global teams and third-party suppliers.

Some specific responsibilities include:

· Proactively manage the availability, integrity and performance of control centre systems, including SCADA platforms, OT servers, communications, data historians and system interfaces.

· Develop, configure, test and maintain Control Centre system functionality, including SCADA applications, HMIs, alarm management, historian systems, interfaces, calculations, reporting and data integrations.

· Maintain, configure, test, patch and upgrade OT and control centre systems in live operational environments, with minimal operational impact.

· Investigate incidents, perform root cause analysis and coordinate resolution with internal teams, vendors and external suppliers.

· Participate in control centre deployment and evolution projects, including design reviews, factory and site acceptance testing, commissioning and operational handover.

· Contribute to global initiatives through collaboration, standardisation and adoption of best practices and global architectures.

· Support the integration of new renewable assets, technologies and data sources into the control centre environment.

· Support OT asset lifecycle management, including obsolescence planning, upgrades and replacement activities.

· Comply with applicable regulatory requirements and OT cybersecurity policies, standards and procedures.

· Manage and implement changes in accordance with the OT Change Management process.

· Develop and maintain accurate technical documentation, procedures, configuration records and system records.


About You

To be successful in this role you will have tertiary qualifications in engineering, automation, IT/OT or similar and strong experience in a similar role within energy or renewables (preferred).

Experience configuring, supporting or administering PcVue SCADA systems will be very well regarded.

Your excellent interpersonal skills allow you to build effective working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders, resulting in exceptional performance.

You will be able to work in a very hands-on, flexible and practical manner while thinking strategically, and you will be comfortable and able to travel interstate to both office and site locations when required.


The Benefits

This is an exceptional career opportunity to join a world leader in renewable energy and join a brand new team and help develop and shape the future of the Operations Control Centre.



Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Donna Ison on +61 0417718763, quoting reference JN -102026-44461. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.description:

job.title: Return to Work & Injury Management Partner
job.description:
About the Company
Our client is a large, purpose-led national organisation with a strong commitment to employee safety, health and wellbeing. With an established and fully resourced injury management function, they offer a collaborative, high-trust environment where team members are supported while given genuine autonomy.

Joining an experienced national team, you’ll manage your own portfolio, partner closely with operational leaders and support employees throughout their recovery and return to work journey. With strong internal support and genuine flexibility, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact within a supportive and people-focused organisation.

About the Role
As a Return to Work & Injury Management Partner, you will manage a portfolio of approximately 60–70 work and non-work-related injury cases, supporting employees from initial notification through recovery, return to work and resolution.

Working closely with injured employees, operational leaders, insurers, medical practitioners and allied health providers, you will develop and drive practical return to work strategies, manage suitable duties and proactively address barriers to recovery.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • End-to-end injury and workers' compensation case management
  • Managing a portfolio of approximately 60–70 active claims
  • Developing and monitoring return to work and recovery strategies
  • Supporting employees through complex or sensitive injury matters
  • Providing advice on Victorian workers' compensation requirements
  • Coordinating suitable duties and rehabilitation plans
  • Partnering with operational leaders, insurers and treating practitioners
  • Proactively managing new claims, statutory requirements and key deadlines
  • Participating in claims reviews and influencing claim strategy
  • Coaching leaders around early intervention and effective return to work practices
  • Maintaining accurate, compliant and confidential case documentation

About You
You will be an experienced injury management professional who combines strong technical knowledge with empathy, organisation and excellent communication skills.

To be successful, you will ideally bring:

  • Minimum 3 years' experience in injury management, return to work and/or workers' compensation
  • Strong knowledge of the Victorian workers' compensation scheme
  • Demonstrated experience managing claims from initial notification through to resolution
  • Confidence managing a busy portfolio and competing priorities
  • Strong stakeholder management across employees, leaders, insurers and health professionals
  • A proactive, self-directed approach with the ability to keep cases progressing
  • Strong interpersonal skills and confidence supporting employees through difficult or distressing circumstances
  • Current Return to Work Coordinator certification, or relevant equivalent experience
  • Ability to obtain a Working with Children Check

Experience within a large, multi-site or operational organisation will be highly regarded; however, industry background is flexible.

The Benefits

  • Permanent opportunity with a large national organisation
  • Port Melbourne location with onsite parking
  • Highly flexible hybrid working model
  • Monday team anchor day, with the balance incorporating WFH and visits to Victorian sites
  • Autonomy to manage your own geographic portfolio
  • Established national injury management team of approximately 18
  • Dedicated administrative support
  • Supportive onboarding and an experienced team member available as a buddy
  • High-trust, collaborative team culture
  • Varied role combining technical case management, employee support and stakeholder partnering


Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact on chantelle.flood@davidsonwp.com, quoting reference JN -102026-44454. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: AO4 Assistant Finance Officer
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson is partnering with a large and highly regarded Queensland Government organisation to recruit an experienced Assistant Finance Officer (Helpdesk).

This organisation provides essential services to communities across Queensland and is supported by a diverse workforce operating across metropolitan and regional locations.

You will join an established corporate services environment where effective financial operations, strong governance and responsive internal support are critical to the organisation’s success.


About the Role

Reporting to the Senior Project Officer, you will be a key member of the team supporting the day-to-day delivery of financial operations and systems.

The position provides helpdesk services, advice and practical support to staff across the organisation, with responsibilities spanning corporate cards, travel allowances, accounts payable and receivable, ExpenseMe Pro and SAP finance systems.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Providing financial helpdesk support and advice to staff on processes, system functions and best practice.
  • Supporting users with ExpenseMe Pro and SAP finance systems, including system access requirements.
  • Investigating and resolving system issues, escalating more complex matters where required.
  • Assisting with training content and user acceptance testing to ensure systems and services meet stakeholder needs.
  • Supporting financial and business administration activities, including revenue and expense management.
  • Preparing monthly reports and reconciliations across finance, corporate card and travel allowance systems.
  • Developing and maintaining financial training resources and user support information.
  • Providing accounting and systems support and recommending solutions that improve the user experience.
  • Contributing to the review and implementation of financial practices, procedures and systems.
  • Supporting continuous improvement initiatives across financial operations.


About You

You will be an experienced finance professional who enjoys combining financial administration with problem-solving, systems support and stakeholder service.

Comfortable working with a range of internal stakeholders, you will be able to translate financial processes and system requirements into clear, practical advice while maintaining a strong focus on accuracy, governance and service delivery.

To be successful, you will ideally bring:

  • Experience within a financial helpdesk, finance operations or systems support environment.
  • Experience supporting end users of finance and travel management systems.
  • Knowledge of accounts payable, accounts receivable and general financial administration processes.
  • Strong reconciliation, reporting and data accuracy skills.
  • Confidence troubleshooting system and user issues.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • The ability to build effective working relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders.
  • A proactive approach to identifying process and service improvements.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities.

Previous experience using SAP ECC for payment management and reporting will be highly regarded.


The Benefits

This is an excellent opportunity to build on your finance and systems experience within a large, complex and purpose-driven environment.

You will benefit from:

  • Permanent flexible full-time employment.
  • Convenient Brisbane CBD location.
  • A varied position spanning finance, systems, reporting and stakeholder support.
  • Exposure to enterprise financial systems and processes.
  • The opportunity to contribute to process and service improvements.
  • A collaborative team environment with a strong focus on quality, governance and customer service.
  • The opportunity to support an organisation delivering important services to communities across Queensland.


If you are a finance professional with strong systems capability who enjoys helping users, resolving problems and improving financial processes, please submit your current resume to apply.

If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Natalee Thorpe (natalee.thorpe@davidsonwp.com), quoting reference JN -102026-44442. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: Test Analyst
job.description:
About the Company

Our client is a large enterprise organisation undertaking a major payroll and workforce management transformation program. The program will deliver a new payroll and workforce management solution across a complex enterprise environment, supporting critical payroll, time and attendance processes and integrations.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Test Analyst to join the broader transformation team and support the testing and implementation of the new payroll and workforce management solution.


The role will focus on testing across payroll, workforce management, timesheeting and time & attendance, including the integrations and end-to-end processes that connect these systems.


Experience with SAP Employee Central Payroll (ECP) / SAP Payroll is highly preferred, with candidates who have worked across large payroll or HR transformation programs particularly well suited.


You will work closely with business, payroll and technology stakeholders to support testing activities, identify and manage defects, validate system functionality and help ensure the solution delivers accurate end-to-end payroll outcomes.

About You

You will be an experienced Test Analyst with a strong background in payroll, HR or workforce management environments. Ideally, you will bring:

  • SAP Employee Central Payroll (ECP) and/or SAP Payroll experience – highly preferred
  • Strong payroll systems testing experience
  • Experience with timesheeting, time & attendance or workforce management solutions
  • Experience testing end-to-end payroll processes and system integrations
  • Experience across large-scale payroll, HR or workforce transformation programs
  • Strong understanding of end-to-end payroll processes
  • Experience working across business, payroll and technology teams
  • Strong functional, integration and end-to-end testing capability
  • Experience identifying, documenting and managing defects through to resolution
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills
  • Experience working within large, complex enterprise environments

Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Dylan Tasker on dylan.tasker@davidsonwp.com , quoting reference JN -102026-44443. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: Change Analyst
job.description:
About the Company
Davidson is partnering with a leading organisation undergoing a significant transformation program. This is an opportunity to join a large-scale migration and support the business through meaningful organisational and operational change.

About the Role
We are seeking an experienced Change Analyst with strong exposure to release, implementation and business readiness activities.

Working across project, technology and business teams, you will support the coordination of change through key release milestones, helping ensure impacted teams are prepared for deployment, go-live and transition into BAU.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Supporting release and implementation planning across key program milestones
  • Coordinating business readiness activities ahead of deployment and go-live
  • Conducting change impact assessments across people, process and technology
  • Tracking implementation actions, risks, dependencies and readiness criteria
  • Supporting stakeholder engagement, communications and training activities
  • Preparing updates, reporting and materials for Steering Committee and governance forums
  • Supporting SteerCo meetings through clear progress reporting, risks, decisions and key implementation updates
  • Working closely with delivery, technology and business teams throughout the release lifecycle
  • Supporting cutover, go-live and post-implementation activities
  • Monitoring adoption and supporting the transition of change into BAU


About You
You will be a hands-on Change Analyst who is comfortable working in a fast-paced implementation environment and coordinating activity across multiple stakeholder groups.

Ideally, you will bring:

  • Previous experience as a Change Analyst, Implementation Analyst or similar
  • Strong experience supporting business readiness, release or implementation activities
  • Experience with change impact assessments, stakeholder engagement and communications
  • Experience preparing reporting or materials for Steering Committees or senior governance forums
  • A strong understanding of the activities required to prepare a business for go-live
  • Experience within banking or broader financial services is highly preferred
  • Exposure to large-scale technology implementations, system releases or transformation programs would be advantageous
  • Strong organisation skills with the ability to manage competing milestones and dependencies

The Benefits

  • Join a large and complex transformation program
  • Work with experienced change and delivery professionals
  • Opportunity to build experience across a significant enterprise implementation
  • Hybrid working arrangements

Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Tara Gearon at tara.gearon@davidsonwp.com, quoting reference JN -102026-44457. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: Workplace Relations Advisor
job.description:
About the Company
Our client is a large and well-established organisation based in Melbourne’s south-east, operating within a complex and highly regulated environment. They are seeking an experienced Workplace Relations professional to provide additional support to their established team during a busy period through to the end of the year.

About the Role
This is an immediate-start contract through to the end of December, with potential for extension.

There is genuine flexibility around the level of this appointment. We are open to experienced Workplace Relations/Employee Relations Advisors and Specialists through to Business Partner and Senior Business Partner level. The scope and complexity of the role can be adapted depending on the successful candidate’s experience.

Key responsibilities may include:

  • End-to-end employee and workplace relations case management
  • Performance management, PIPs, conduct and disciplinary matters
  • Workplace investigations and sensitive employee matters
  • Grievances, disputes and conflict resolution
  • Enterprise Agreement, Award and policy interpretation
  • Coaching and advising managers through workplace matters
  • Drafting and reviewing formal correspondence, including warning and outcome letters
  • Supporting union and employee representative matters
  • Maintaining accurate case documentation and records

The role is based in Dandenong with 3 days onsite and 2 days WFH. Some travel to other sites may be required depending on individual cases and matters.

About You

You may be an experienced Workplace Relations Advisor looking for broader exposure, an established ER/WR Specialist, or a senior Business Partner interested in a hands-on short-term assignment.

Most importantly, you will have genuine hands-on Workplace Relations experience and the confidence to manage employee matters through to resolution.

You will ideally bring:

  • Strong Workplace Relations / Employee Relations case management experience
  • Experience across performance, conduct, investigations and complex employee matters
  • Knowledge of Enterprise Agreements, Awards and relevant employment legislation
  • Confidence coaching and advising managers through sensitive matters

Davidson is partnering with a growing Australian organisation operating across resource recovery, recycling and secure asset processing to appoint a National Operations Manager – Resource Recovery.

Reporting to the General Manager and leading approximately 3–4 Site Managers, you will oversee a growing network of processing facilities across Australia.

This is a hands-on leadership role focused on making the national operation work efficiently, consistently and commercially – ensuring valuable assets and recovered materials are accurately tracked, effectively processed and moved through the right channels.

The opportunity

You will take ownership of operational performance across multiple sites, with responsibility for:

  • Leading and developing Site Managers across the national network

  • Maintaining strong safety, environmental and regulatory standards

About you

Your background could come from e-waste, metals recycling, resource recovery, secure asset recovery, reverse logistics, waste management, industrial processing, warehousing or logistics.

Direct recycling experience would be advantageous, but the priority is finding an accomplished operational leader with strong capability across:

  • Logistics – transport, material movements, warehousing, scheduling and multi-site coordination

Exposure to commodity pricing, recovered-material sales or downstream processors would be beneficial but isn't essential.

Leadership with purpose

The organisation combines commercial and environmental performance with a strong social purpose, creating meaningful employment and development opportunities for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.

Experience working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people would be valued but isn't essential. Alignment with the organisation's purpose and a willingness to undertake cultural competency training are important.

job.title: People Experience Business Partner | Zoos Victoria
job.description:
$110,000–$117,000 + super | Fixed term to 30 June 2027
Hybrid working | Parkville, Werribee & Healesville

There aren’t too many HR Business Partner roles where your stakeholder group spans frontline operations, corporate functions and conservation programs – or where your workplace might include a zoo!

Davidson is delighted to be partnering with Zoos Victoria to recruit an experienced People Experience Business Partner to join their team on a fixed-term basis through to 30 June 2027.

Zoos Victoria is a purpose-led, not-for-profit Victorian Government statutory authority operating Melbourne Zoo, Werribee Open Range Zoo, Healesville Sanctuary and Kyabram Fauna Park. Its work is centred on conservation, threatened species management and fighting extinction.

The opportunity
You’ll join Zoos Victoria at an important point of organisational change as the People Experience team transitions from a property-based model to a new centralised portfolio structure.

This is a broad, hands-on HR Business Partner role supporting a diverse portfolio across Assets & Presentations, Conservation & Science and Finance.

That means your stakeholders could range from highly operational and frontline teams across maintenance, horticulture and other site-based functions, through to professional, corporate and academic environments.

The role will suit an HRBP who enjoys variety, is comfortable working close to the business and can adapt their partnering style to different stakeholder groups.

What you’ll be doing
You’ll provide practical, trusted HR advice across the full employee lifecycle, including:

  • Partnering with operational, frontline and corporate leaders across your portfolio
  • Managing employee relations and industrial relations matters
  • Working confidently within a unionised environment, particularly with the United Workers Union
  • Coaching and building the capability of frontline managers as the organisation moves to a new operating model
  • Supporting managers through performance, grievances and complex people matters
  • Providing advice on employment legislation, EBAs, awards and relevant industrial instruments
  • Supporting workforce planning, organisational change and cultural initiatives
  • Providing broader generalist HR support across recruitment, HR processes and day-to-day people matters
  • Navigating HR systems and supporting the business through the transition to Dayforce
  • Contributing to broader People Experience projects and the implementation of the new operating model

About you
We’re looking for a well-rounded HR Business Partner who can operate confidently across both operational and professional environments.

You’ll bring:

  • Strong generalist HR Business Partner experience
  • Sound ER/IR capability and confidence dealing with complex employee matters
  • Experience working with frontline and/or operational workforces
  • Experience in a unionised environment
  • Strong stakeholder management and manager coaching skills
  • The ability to build credibility with people at all levels and work independently
  • Confidence adapting your approach between operational, corporate and professional stakeholder groups
  • Strong judgement, problem-solving ability and resilience
  • Good HR systems capability and the ability to learn new technology quickly
  • Tertiary qualifications in Human Resources or another relevant discipline
  • A current driver's licence

You don't need to have worked specifically in a trades environment however, we're interested in people who have genuine experience partnering with frontline, operational and unionised workforces. Experience in government, local government or similarly complex environments could translate particularly well.

Working at Zoos Victoria
This role operates across a genuinely unique environment.

The general working model is approximately three days onsite and two days working from home, with flexibility available from commencement.

Your onsite days will include time at the Parkville/Melbourne Zoo office, as well as across other Zoos Victoria properties including Werribee Open Range Zoo and Healesville Sanctuary.

The role generally operates around 9.00am–5.00pm, with flexibility around start and finish times provided business requirements are met.

Why Zoos Victoria?
This is an opportunity to join an organisation where the purpose is incredibly clear – the work you do directly supports an organisation focused on conservation and fighting extinction.

You'll also get exposure to a breadth of HR work that is difficult to find in a single role: operational and frontline partnering, union and ER/IR matters, professional and academic stakeholders, organisational change and HR transformation.

You'll join an experienced and collaborative People Experience team that values trust, autonomy and supporting each other through complex work.

Salary sacrifice arrangements are also available, including options relating to superannuation and vehicles.

The details
Salary: $110,000–$117,000 + super
Employment: Fixed term via Zoos Victoria payroll
Duration: ASAP to 30 June 2027
Location: Parkville, with regular attendance across Werribee and Healesville
Working arrangement: Approximately 3 days onsite / 2 days WFH

A Police Check and Working with Children Check will be required.

Ready for something a little different?
If you're an experienced HR Business Partner who likes being close to the business, can stay calm when things get complex and enjoys helping managers navigate change, we'd love to hear from you.

And yes – working at Zoos Victoria really is as interesting as it sounds.

To apply
Please apply with current resume in Microsoft Word format only (.doc or .docx). If you would like to have a confidential discussion, please contact Catherine Lyttle. Want to know more about Davidson? Visit us at www.davidsonwp.com

Davidson acknowledges the Traditional Custodians of the lands on which we work and live. We are also committed to equal opportunity and strive to promote diversity, inclusion, belonging, flexibility, and accessibility in all that we do.

job.title: Investigations Officers | APS5 & APS6
job.description:
Federal Government | Canberra ACT | $52.78 to $65.48/hr + super


Multiple positions | Regulatory investigations | Up to 12 months


If you have established experience in investigations, regulatory compliance, intelligence or related work, this is an opportunity to apply your expertise to complex matters within a Commonwealth regulatory environment.

Davidson Executive & Talent is recruiting multiple Investigations Officers at APS5 and APS6 equivalent levels for an expanding regulatory function in Canberra.

These are experienced-level roles requiring strong investigative and analytical capability, sound judgement and confidence working with complex evidence, financial information, data and intelligence.

Appointment at APS5 or APS6 level will depend on your experience, capability and the level of responsibility you have previously undertaken.


The opportunity

You will investigate, or support investigations into, potential non-compliance and avoidance activity within a complex regulatory environment.

You will draw on information from multiple sources to identify patterns, risks and potential issues. Your findings will help decision-makers determine where further compliance or regulatory action may be required.

Depending on your experience and level, you will:

  • Conduct or support complex regulatory investigations
  • Gather, review, analyse and document evidence and information
  • Examine financial records and other documentation to identify discrepancies, gaps and potential issues
  • Use data and intelligence to identify high-risk behaviours, entities and activities
  • Identify patterns and indicators of potential non-compliance
  • Apply risk-based approaches to investigation activities
  • Develop clear, evidence-based findings and advice
  • Prepare investigation reports, briefs and correspondence for decision-makers
  • Contribute to targeted compliance and regulatory strategies
  • Work collaboratively with internal stakeholders and other team members
  • At APS6 level, independently manage more complex investigations and provide guidance and support to junior team members

APS6 officers will work with greater autonomy and accountability. You will be expected to progress complex investigations, exercise sound judgement and produce high-quality material that can support regulatory decision-making.


Who we're looking for

These are not entry-level opportunities. We are looking for experienced professionals with backgrounds in one or more of the following areas:

  • Government investigations
  • Regulatory investigations
  • Compliance investigations
  • Fraud and integrity
  • Financial investigations
  • Intelligence and risk analysis
  • Regulatory enforcement
  • Audit or forensic review
  • Commonwealth, state or territory regulatory agencies
  • Other evidence-based investigative environments

You will bring strong analytical and investigative capability, sound judgement and clear written communication skills.

You should be comfortable working through complex information, identifying what does and does not add up, documenting your findings and producing evidence-based advice that can withstand scrutiny.

For APS6 opportunities, we are particularly interested in candidates who can independently progress complex investigations, apply risk-based decision-making and prepare high-quality briefs and reports. Experience guiding or supporting less experienced officers will also be important.

A Certificate IV in Government Investigations (PSP40416) is highly desirable. Candidates with strong relevant experience who are willing to undertake the qualification may also be considered, with AEC support available to complete the qualification.

What's on offer?

  • Multiple APS5 and APS6 equivalent opportunities
  • APS5: $52.78 to $57.84 per hour + super
  • APS6: $58.42 to $65.48 per hour + super
  • Canberra location
  • Initial engagement of up to 12 months
  • Expected commencement November 2026
  • Work within a significant Commonwealth regulatory environment
  • Potential flexible working arrangements, subject to agreement

Essential requirements

To be considered, you must:

  • Be an Australian citizen
  • Be able to obtain and maintain a Baseline security clearance
  • Be willing to undertake a National Police Check and required pre-employment screening
  • Meet strict political neutrality and conflict-of-interest requirements

If you are an experienced investigations, compliance or intelligence professional looking to apply your expertise in a Commonwealth regulatory setting, we would like to hear from you.

Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Joel Hall at joel.hall@davidsonwp.com, quoting reference JN -102026-44437. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: Data Analyst
job.description:
JOB TITLE: Data Analyst (Microsoft Dynamics CRM)
JOB LOCATION: Melbourne, VIC (Hybrid)
JOB DURATION: 6-month contract

About the Role:
We are seeking a skilled and detail-oriented Data Analyst to join our team. The ideal candidate will have 3-6 years of experience in data migration, analysis, and transformation projects, with a strong background in Microsoft Fabric and business intelligence (BI) tools. This role involves ensuring the seamless migration of data between systems while maintaining data quality, integrity, and performance standards.

Key Responsibilities:
Data analysis and mapping

  • Analyse source and target systems to understand data structures, relationships and business meaning.
  • Profile source data to identify quality issues, duplicates, gaps and inconsistencies.
  • Create and maintain source-to-target mappings.
  • Work with business stakeholders to define transformation and cleansing rules.

Migration support

  • Write SQL queries to analyse data and test transformation logic.
  • Work with data engineers to make sure transformation rules are implemented correctly in Fabric.
  • Run and monitor migration loads and investigate failures or unexpected results.
  • Support cutover activities, including readiness checks and post-cutover validation.

Testing, validation and reconciliation

  • Plan and run pre- and post-migration testing.
  • Reconcile source and target data using row counts, totals and field-level comparisons.
  • Log, track and follow up data issues through to resolution, and escalate risks early.
  • Build Power BI reports to track migration progress, data quality and reconciliation results.

Data quality and governance

  • Help business owners decide how to handle data quality issues, such as cleansing, excluding or accepting them.
  • Handle sensitive and personal information in line with the Privacy Act 1988 and internal data policies.
  • Support governance activities such as data definitions, ownership and classification.

Collaboration and documentation

  • Act as the link between business stakeholders and the technical team on data requirements.
  • Maintain clear documentation, covering mappings, business rules, test results and issue logs.
  • Provide regular status updates to the project team.

Key Selection Criteria:

  • Please address each of the following in your application, in [no more than two pages].
  • Demonstrated experience in data migration or data analysis projects, including data profiling and source-to-target mapping.
  • Strong SQL skills for analysing, validating and reconciling data.
  • Your experience with Microsoft Dynamics CRM.
  • Experience building Power BI reports and dashboards.
  • Experience working with Microsoft Fabric or similar Microsoft data platforms (e.g. Azure Synapse, SQL Server).
  • Strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to investigating and resolving data issues.
  • Excellent communication skills, including gathering requirements and explaining data issues to non-technical stakeholders.

Education & Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, or related field.
  • 3-6 years of experience as a Data Analyst, preferably with Microsoft Dynamics CRM.

Other Skills:

  • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to troubleshoot technical issues.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a cross-functional team.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Knowledge of Agile methodologies.
  • Relevant Data/Business Analysis certifications.



Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Bidisha Swayamprava on Bidisha.Swayamprava@davidsonwp.com, quoting reference JN -102026-44447. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

Founded in 1991, we listen closely, understand the challenge and apply practical, experience-led thinking that helps organisations move forward with confidence. Our focus is on bringing clarity to complexity and supporting stronger, more resilient futures.

At Davidson, you will be part of a business evolving with the challenges our clients face. You will design and govern integration solutions using the Microsoft Azure integration stack, including Logic Apps, Service Bus, API Management and Power Automate. You will also provide architectural oversight of vendor designs, support delivery teams through build and implementation, and ensure integration decisions align with both immediate program requirements and the organisation's longer-term technology strategy.

You will ideally bring:

  • Strong Azure integration architecture experience, particularly Logic Apps, Service Bus and API Management

  • Strong knowledge of APIs, messaging, event-driven architecture and enterprise integration patterns
  • Experience integrating cloud, SaaS and legacy enterprise applications
  • Exposure to Dynamics 365 and Dataverse integrations, without needing to be a D365 specialist

  • Strong architecture governance and technical design capabilities
  • Experience working across large digital transformation programs involving multiple systems and vendors

Working across business and technology teams, you will assess the existing platform, identify improvement opportunities and translate business requirements into practical, sustainable CRM solutions. You will provide functional solution design expertise across Dynamics 365 Customer Service, Dataverse and Power Platform, while supporting integrations with the organisation's contact-centre technology.




A key focus will be improving the interaction between Dynamics 365 and Amazon Connect, ensuring customer interactions, cases and data flow effectively between platforms.




You will also act as an internal Dynamics 365 SME, providing design guidance, challenging vendor recommendations where appropriate and helping establish stronger internal ownership and governance of the CRM platform.




Key responsibilities will include:

  • Assess and optimise the existing Dynamics 365 CRM environment.

  • Support Dynamics 365, Dataverse and contact-centre integrations.

  • Support testing, defect management and release readiness.
  • Review vendor solutions and provide functional design assurance.
  • Improve CRM processes, data quality, adoption and ways of working.

About You

You will ideally bring:

  • Strong Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM functional experience.
  • Experience with Dynamics 365 Customer Service.
  • Strong knowledge of Dataverse, including tables, relationships, security, workflows, forms and views.
  • Experience designing and configuring Dynamics 365 solutions.

job.description:
An established and growing construction and trade services business is looking for an experienced Estimating Manager to strengthen its construction and fitout capability.

This isn’t a role where you’ll step away from estimating to purely manage people. You’ll be actively involved in tenders while helping improve the overall quality and sophistication of the estimating function.

You’ll take responsibility for:

  • Leading and preparing construction and fitout estimates and tenders from initial review through to submission
  • Producing accurate cost plans, take-offs, labour and material build-ups and subcontractor pricing
  • Improving the quality of tender submissions, including methodologies, programmes, qualifications and supporting documentation

  • Providing practical guidance and mentoring to two developing estimators

Ideally, you’ll bring:

  • Strong recent estimating experience across commercial construction, fitout or refurbishment projects
  • Confidence managing tenders from initial documentation through to final submission
  • Strong understanding of construction costs, subcontractor packages, programmes and commercial risk
  • Experience producing high-quality tender methodologies and documentation
  • The ability to review and improve estimating processes and systems
  • The capability to mentor less experienced estimators without needing to formally “manage” them
  • A calm, considered and cooperative approach

Why consider this opportunity?

You’ll be joining a business with ambitious growth plans at a point where you can have a genuine impact on how the estimating function develops.

Rather than inheriting a rigid corporate structure, you’ll have the opportunity to bring your experience, improve systems and standards, develop two promising estimators and help shape a function that will support the next stage of the organisation’s growth.

job.title: Compliance & Regulation Officers | APS5 & APS6
job.description:
Federal Government | Melbourne | $82,336 to $102,152/annum + super




Multiple positions | Up to 12 months | Major Commonwealth regulatory program




If you have established experience in compliance, audit, assurance, accounting or finance, this is an opportunity to apply that expertise in a complex Commonwealth regulatory environment.

Davidson Executive & Talent is recruiting multiple Compliance & Regulation Officers at APS5 and APS6 equivalent levels for an expanding regulatory function in Melbourne.

These are experienced-level roles requiring strong analytical capability, sound judgement and confidence working with detailed financial, regulatory or legislative information.

Appointment at APS5 or APS6 level will depend on your experience, capability and the complexity of work you have previously managed.

The opportunity

You will contribute to important regulatory and financial compliance activities within a complex legislative environment.

Your work will involve reviewing financial information, undertaking compliance assessments and identifying risks or potential non-compliance. You will help ensure decisions and financial processes are accurate, defensible and supported by evidence.

Depending on your experience and level, you will:

  • Review financial disclosures, claims and supporting documentation for accuracy, completeness and compliance
  • Undertake structured compliance reviews and assessments
  • Analyse financial and other information to identify discrepancies, risks and potential non-compliance
  • Interpret legislation, policy and procedures and apply them to individual matters
  • Gather and analyse information from multiple sources
  • Prepare clear written advice, correspondence, reports and briefs
  • Engage with internal stakeholders and external participants
  • Support the accurate administration and processing of funding
  • Manage competing priorities while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail
  • At APS6 level, independently manage more complex assessments, exercise sound judgement and provide guidance to junior team members

The underlying AEC position descriptions identify financial audit and assurance experience, and qualifications or experience in accounting, commerce, finance or related disciplines, as highly desirable for the compliance stream.

Who we're looking for

These are not entry-level opportunities. We are looking for experienced professionals who can bring established capability in one or more of the following areas:

  • Regulatory or legislative compliance
  • Financial compliance
  • Audit and assurance
  • Accounting or finance
  • Risk and controls
  • Government regulatory programs
  • Financial assessments or reviews
  • Grants, funding or payment assurance
  • Complex case assessment or administrative decision-making

You will be analytical and methodical, with the judgement to work through detailed financial or regulatory matters. Strong written communication and stakeholder engagement skills are important, as is the ability to reach well-reasoned conclusions based on evidence.

For APS6 opportunities, we are particularly interested in candidates who have independently managed complex work, exercised judgement in a regulatory or assurance environment, and supported or guided less experienced team members.



What's on offer?

  • Multiple APS5 and APS6 equivalent opportunities
  • APS5: $82,336 to $90,234 per annum + super
  • APS6: $91,140 to $102,152 per annum + super
  • Melbourne location
  • Initial engagement of up to 12 months
  • Expected commencement November 2026
  • Opportunity to contribute to a significant Commonwealth regulatory program
  • Potential flexible working arrangements, subject to agreement

Essential requirements

To be considered, you must:

  • Be an Australian citizen
  • Be able to obtain and maintain a Baseline security clearance
  • Be willing to undertake a National Police Check and required pre-employment screening
  • Meet strict political neutrality and conflict-of-interest requirements

If you are an experienced compliance, audit, assurance, accounting or finance professional looking to apply your expertise in a Commonwealth regulatory setting, we would like to hear from you.

job.title: General Counsel and Director, Legal Services
job.description:
• Full-time, ongoing role (salary grade: VPS 7.2)
  • Provide independent legal advice and shape legal strategy
  • Lead a high-performing legal team and contribute directly to safeguarding Victoria's democratic processes.

The Victorian Electoral Commission (VEC) is an independent and impartial body established under the Electoral Act 2002 (Vic). The VEC has 2 important roles in Victoria’s democracy: running elections and regulating elections.

The General Counsel and Director, Legal Services is a pivotal senior leadership role reporting to the Assistant Commissioner, Electoral Integrity and Regulation. As the VEC's principal legal advisor, you will provide expert, independent and timely legal advice and guidance to the Electoral Commissioner, Deputy Electoral Commissioner, executives and senior leaders in a complex, politically sensitive and often time-critical environment. You will lead the in-house Legal Services function and oversee legal strategy, disputes and litigation, legal support for electoral services, regulatory compliance and enforcement, legislative reform, external counsel, budget management, quality assurance and corporate governance.

This role will be required to initiate, develop and nurture partnerships with internal and external stakeholders and decision-makers, and negotiate solutions to complex problems, including in relation to major projects and high-value commercial matters. You will also deputise for the Assistant Commissioner during election delivery and in response to significant issues, risks or threats.

Success in this role will require a senior legal professional with expert knowledge and leading practice in administrative law, constitutional law, government law, and regulatory compliance and enforcement. You will have substantial experience and pride yourself in your ability to provide high-quality legal advice, analysis and research; managing and developing lawyers at various stages of practice; and leading complex legal matters, including appearing as solicitor-advocate, instructing counsel or overseeing external legal advisors. You will exercise sound judgement and influence solutions to complex problems in a busy and politically sensitive environment. You will have experience or a solid understanding of public administration, assurance, integrity, crisis management, risk management, statutory reporting, and the Victorian Public Sector, including Cabinet and Parliamentary processes and machinery of government.

Your leadership will build trust, foster collaboration, and support a high-performing, inclusive and capable in-house legal team. Experience within an electoral management body or related government policy environment is desirable, but not essential. You must be admitted to practise law in Australia and hold a current Victorian practising certificate as a government legal practitioner, or be eligible to obtain one before commencing. You must also have at least seven years of post-admission experience in legal practice as a lawyer in a common law jurisdiction.This is an opportunity to make a significant contribution to safeguarding Victoria's democracy while working with an organisation committed to independence, integrity, fairness and inclusion.

The VEC offers a safe, modern, and accessible workplace and a hybrid working environment, which is predominantly 2 days in the office each week. Additional days in the office will likely be required during operational peaks. Setting employees up for success is a priority, as is the health and wellbeing of employees. Elections are exciting and lively, and the VEC is open to the challenge of a changing environment. During major election events or key programs of work, extra hours will be required but know you will be helping to safeguard Victoria’s democracy.

The VEC welcomes applications from people of diverse backgrounds and is committed to making reasonable adjustments for applicants and employees.

In accordance with section 17A of the Electoral Act 2002 (Vic), the VEC will ask preferred applicants to disclose specific political activities that could compromise the perceived independence of the organisation. Appointment will be made subject to satisfactory completion and assessment of a Disclosure of Political Activities form. More information is available here:

https://www.vec.vic.gov.au/work-with-us/disclosure-of-political-activities

job.title: Director Life Sciences - Zoos Victoria
job.description:
• Lead the organisation’s core animal care, health and planning functions
  • Shape world class animal welfare, conservation and species management outcomes
  • Join a purpose led, values driven organisation committed to fighting extinction

Zoos Victoria is a not-for-profit Victorian Government statutory authority operating Melbourne Zoo, Werribee Open Range Zoo, Healesville Sanctuary and Kyabram Fauna Park. Caring for more than 5,500 animals, Zoos Victoria is committed to ensuring no Victorian terrestrial species goes extinct on its watch.

With a vision to be a world leading zoo based conservation organisation, Zoos Victoria delivers conservation programs, wildlife recovery initiatives, emergency wildlife response and partnerships with communities, research institutions, conservation organisations and sister zoos nationally and internationally. The organisation’s 2030 Strategy and Development and Growth Plan provide a clear focus on conservation impact, organisational capability and long term sustainability.

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and contributing as a member of the Executive Team, the Director Life Sciences will provide strategic leadership across Animal Care, Animal Health and Animal Planning. This is an exciting opportunity to bring Life Sciences together as a more integrated and influential organisational function, ensuring consistently high standards of animal welfare, husbandry, veterinary care, biosecurity and species management across all sites.

This is a significant change leadership role. You will help shape and communicate the organisation’s change narrative, bring people on the journey and develop a contemporary approach to how Life Sciences operates into the future. With strong technical capability already established across the team, you will build on this foundation, strengthen integration and help create something new. Working closely with leaders across conservation, visitor experience, assets and operations, you will provide strategic and operational advice to the CEO, Board and Executive Team. You will oversee performance, financial management, workforce capability, risk, compliance, safety and continuous improvement across the portfolio.

The successful candidate will bring deep credibility in Life Sciences, animal management, veterinary care, conservation or a related specialist environment, together with experience leading complex teams and functions. You will be a strategic, people focused leader who combines technical credibility with curiosity, humility and the ability to build trust. Your capacity to listen, understand the organisation and lead through change will be critical, as will your ability to create a compelling vision for the future. Experience in zoological, wildlife, conservation, captive collections, animal management, public sector or another highly regulated environment will be highly regarded. A relevant tertiary qualification and formal leadership or management experience is essential.

This is an opportunity to join Zoos Victoria at a pivotal point in its development and play a defining role in shaping its next chapter as a world leading conservation organisation.

job.title: Head of Data & Technology - Brisbane Lions
job.description:
Davidson is proud to partner with the Brisbane Lions Football Club to appoint their new Head of Data & Technology. This is a pivotal time to join one of Australia's premier sporting clubs, as technology, data and sport converge to shape future growth and success across the organisation, both on and off the field. Reporting directly to the COO, this role will lead the Club's combined Technology, Data and AI agenda.

About the Company

This is not simply a role focused on keeping the lights on. The Lions are entering their next stage of technology, data and AI maturity, giving you the opportunity to genuinely influence what comes next.

  • Shape the Club's future technology strategy.
  • Lead its growing data and AI agenda.
  • Build and mature the technology function.
  • Work across a unique and highly visible organisation.
  • See the impact of your work across the broader Brisbane Lions business.

About the Role

This is a rare opportunity to lead technology, data and innovation for one of Australia's most recognised sporting organisations at an exciting point in its evolution. This is a hands-on technology leadership role: you will lead the strategic direction while staying close to delivery across IT operations, cybersecurity, business systems, data, AI and digital innovation.

With the Club moving into its next stage of technology and data maturity, you will shape the roadmap, accelerate the use of AI and data across the business, and build the technology capability required for the future.


What you will be doing

The Lions operate a diverse technology environment with systems spanning internal, cloud and third-party solutions. The role will work closely with the AFL and key technology partners to leverage the existing technology and data ecosystem, maximise current infrastructure and achieve strong commercial outcomes.

  • Lead the delivery of the Club's Technology, Data and Innovation strategy.
  • Lead IT operations across systems, infrastructure, networks and applications.
  • Enhance and support the Football department's capability through technology.
  • Manage the Club's managed service provider and broader technology vendor ecosystem.
  • Strengthen cybersecurity, technology risk and governance.
  • Drive greater maturity across data, analytics and data governance.
  • Lead the Club's adoption of AI, including governance and practical use cases.
  • Partner with the Executive team to identify technology and digital opportunities.
  • Manage competing priorities across a fast-moving and complex organisation.
  • Work closely with the AFL and key technology partners.
  • Lead and develop the internal technology team.

About You

We are looking for a highly engaging, commercially minded and hands-on technology leader who can operate at both a strategic and practical level. You will be comfortable influencing senior stakeholders, making clear trade-offs, staying close to delivery and translating technology opportunities into meaningful business outcomes.

  • Tertiary qualifications in Information Technology, Data Sceince, Business or related fields.
  • Senior leadership experience across Technology, IT, Data and/or Digital Transformation.
  • Broad enterprise technology and business systems experience.
  • Strong managed service provider and vendor management capability.
  • Knowledge of cybersecurity, technology risk and governance.
  • Experience developing and executing technology roadmaps.
  • Understanding of data strategy, governance and analytics.
  • Exposure to, or a strong understanding of, AI and emerging technology.
  • Strong commercial judgement and prioritisation skills.
  • Excellent executive and stakeholder engagement.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary technology teams.
  • Sporting or AFL industry experience would be advantageous but is not essential.

The Benefits

  • 2 x memberships per season for both AFL and AFLW homes games
  • Discounts on Lions merchandise and our on-site café
  • Access to our on-site gym
  • Free parking at Brighton Homes Arena
  • Discounts with some of our partners including New Balance and TotalFusion Lions
  • Regular employee wellbeing and cultural initiatives throughout the year

If you are a hands-on technology leader looking for something beyond the traditional corporate environment, this is an opportunity to make your mark off the field and help shape the future of the Brisbane Lions.

The Brisbane Lions Football Club is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from individuals of diverse backgrounds to apply. This includes, but is not limited to, those from the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, Culturally and Linguistically Diverse and LGBTIQ communities.

We are committed to protecting the safety and wellbeing of children and young people. It is essential that anyone involved with the Brisbane Lions Football Club understands their responsibility in relation to child safety and supports such an environment.

job.title: Service Desk Analyst
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson Technology are working with a leading Federal Government Agency to secure an experienced Service Desk Analyst to support end users of IT systems and services.


About the Role

As the Service Desk Analyst, you will provide responsive, high-quality frontline ICT support as the first point of contact for users, investigating, diagnosing and resolving incidents and service requests across desktop systems, applications, hardware, mobile devices, peripherals and the agency’s Standard Operating Environment. You will manage and track support activities in accordance with ITIL principles, provision and configure new equipment and services, manage faulty or obsolete devices, and provide professional onsite assistance for complex technical issues, meetings, events, audiovisual and video conferencing requirements. You will also provide specialist technical support for digital court prosecutions, including setting up, operating and troubleshooting courtroom technology and assisting with basic video and audio preparation to ensure the reliable presentation of digital evidence. You will work independently to resolve issues using a logical and methodical approach while managing competing priorities and maintaining a strong customer-service focus for legal and corporate staff. You will communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, collaborate with colleagues through knowledge sharing and continuous improvement, and ensure all ICT support activities comply with relevant Australian Government security policies, standards and procedures. You will be expected to take ownership of your work, meet deadlines, adapt quickly to new technologies and changing priorities, and proactively identify practical solutions that support reliable ICT service delivery across the agency.


About You

To be successful in this role, will be an experienced Service Desk Analyst with demonstrated Level 1 service desk and onsite support experience, bringing strong technical proficiency across a broad range of IT systems and the ability to apply this knowledge to effectively investigate, diagnose and resolve day-to-day ICT issues. You will have well-developed analytical and problem-solving skills, using a logical approach and creative thinking to identify practical solutions and achieve timely outcomes for users. You will possess excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical information clearly and professionally to both technical and non-technical stakeholders while maintaining a strong customer-service focus. You will be comfortable working as part of a geographically dispersed team, collaborating remotely, sharing knowledge and supporting colleagues to deliver consistent frontline ICT services across multiple locations. You will demonstrate personal accountability for progressing work, managing priorities, meeting deadlines and following issues through to resolution. You will also be adaptable and quick to learn new technologies, systems and processes, responding positively to changing priorities and uncertainty while demonstrating the resilience, initiative and proactive approach required within a fast-paced national Service Desk environment.

This role requires Australian Citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain NV1 security clearance (with potential for higher clearance if required) and a national police check.


The Benefits

You will be offered an excellent hourly rate on a 6-month contract in a hybrid working environment and the option of 2 x 6-month extensions.


Please submit your current resume to apply. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: Senior Consultant - Business Advisory
job.description:
About Davidson

Davidson is one of Australia’s leading workplace performance companies. For over 30 years, we have partnered with public and private sector clients to enhance workplace performance.


Davidson Business Advisory delivers pragmatic, outcome-focused advice grounded in industry knowledge and consulting expertise. We work alongside clients to achieve measurable and sustainable impact across Strategy & Operations, Transformation Delivery and Talent & Leadership Advisory. Our experienced team combines practical insight with proven consulting methodologies to help organisations navigate transformation, strengthen performance and create sustainable outcomes.


About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Consultant to join our Business Advisory team, helping clients solve complex organisational challenges and enhance workplace performance.

Reporting to a Senior Partner, you will take ownership of consulting workstreams, combining financial and commercial analysis, structured problem-solving and stakeholder insight to deliver practical, measurable outcomes.

You will support and increasingly lead stakeholder interviews and workshops, engage directly with client stakeholders and translate complex information into clear, practical recommendations. As your capability develops, you will take on increasingly complex work and greater responsibility for day-to-day client relationships.


What You’ll Be Doing

  • Manage defined consulting workstreams with increasing independence, maintaining quality, scope and agreed timeframes.
  • Undertake financial and operational analysis, research, data analysis and benchmarking to identify key value drivers and develop evidence-based recommendations.
  • Facilitate stakeholder interviews, workshops and discussions with executive, management and operational audiences.
  • Develop clear, compelling reports, presentations and other client deliverables tailored to the audience.
  • Build trusted client relationships through professionalism, responsiveness, sound judgement and genuine care.
  • Work collaboratively with Senior Partners and multidisciplinary project teams to deliver high-quality outcomes.
  • Contribute to proposals, client presentations and broader business development opportunities.
  • Identify opportunities to extend client value through additional advisory services where appropriate.
  • Contribute to thought leadership, research, consulting methodologies and intellectual property.
  • Share knowledge and provide guidance to Consultants and Graduates, helping strengthen capability across the team.
  • Bring curiosity and contemporary thinking to organisational and workplace challenges while maintaining commercial discipline in project delivery.

What We’re Looking For

You will bring experience from management consulting, business advisory or a comparable professional services environment, with strong financial analysis capability and demonstrated experience across transformation or strategy engagements.

You will ideally demonstrate:

  • Strong financial analysis skills, with the ability to analyse financial and operational data, identify key value drivers and translate findings into commercially sound recommendations.
  • Demonstrated experience in either transformation or strategy, with the ability to contribute to complex engagements and deliver practical, sustainable outcomes.
  • Experience delivering consulting engagements involving research, analysis, stakeholder engagement and workshop facilitation.
  • Strong critical-thinking and problem-solving capability, with the ability to structure complex problems and develop evidence-based recommendations.
  • Well-developed written and verbal communication skills, including high-quality reports, presentations and client documentation.
  • Confidence engaging and facilitating discussions with executive, management and operational stakeholders.
  • Strong commercial awareness and an understanding of scope, efficiency, quality and value in consulting delivery.
  • A relevant tertiary qualification in Business, Commerce, Human Resources, Psychology, Public Policy or a related discipline.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft PowerPoint, Excel, Word, and Canva highly regarded.

Experience across organisational transformation, strategy, workforce, leadership or operating model engagements would be highly regarded, as would postgraduate qualifications or relevant consulting, project management or change management certifications.

Above all, we are looking for someone who is curious about how organisations and people perform, takes pride in producing excellent work and wants to continue developing as a trusted adviser.


Why Join Davidson

At Davidson, we believe when people thrive, organisations thrive. You will be part of a collaborative, value-driven organisation putting people at the centre of its success. We offer the autonomy to make decisions, supported by access to senior leadership and a lean operating model that clears the path rather than clogs it.

  • A national brand with strong market presence and long-term client relationships.
  • A flexible, hybrid work environment.
  • A culture defined by purpose, excellence, care and opportunity.
  • Direct access to decision makers through a flat, agile structure.
  • Learning and development opportunities tailored to your career goals.
  • Recognition programs celebrating individual and team contributions.
  • Fun things we do include – high achievers' lunches, monthly celebration hours, values awards, steak & chips nights.

Ready to step into your next chapter?

If you are looking to build on your consulting experience, work directly with experienced leaders and help clients solve meaningful people and organisational challenges, we would welcome the opportunity to hear from you.

Apply today to join Davidson as our next Senior Consultant – Business Advisory.

job.title: Information Architecture & Solution Readiness Project Manager
