job.title: Business Analysts - ERP / Transformation
job.description:
The opportunity

We are looking for experienced Business Analysts to join the Davidson Technology Consulting team in Brisbane.

These roles will add capacity to an existing business and technology transformation program through to December 2026. You will work as part of the Davidson team, supporting business analysis across discovery, process analysis, requirements, testing and implementation.

We're looking for Business Analysts who do more than document what stakeholders ask for.

You will think critically, challenge constructively and identify the underlying business problem before moving towards a solution. You will help stakeholders separate requirements from preferences, future state from current state, and business value from noise.

That means asking the right questions, testing assumptions and helping stakeholders reach clear, practical decisions. Your role is to understand what the business needs to achieve, then translate that into clear, well-defined and testable requirements.

What you will do

You will:

  • Lead and support discovery to understand the underlying business problem, objectives, constraints and desired outcomes.
  • Elicit, analyse, document and validate business and functional requirements.
  • Distinguish genuine business requirements from preferences and proposed solutions.
  • Challenge assumptions constructively and help stakeholders evaluate what is needed to achieve the intended outcome.
  • Bring structure and clarity to ambiguous or incomplete information.
  • Develop current-state and future-state process maps, workflows and business rules.
  • Identify dependencies, risks, gaps and impacts across people, process, technology and data.
  • Define clear, testable requirements and acceptance criteria.
  • Maintain requirements traceability through delivery and testing.
  • Facilitate workshops with business and technology stakeholders.
  • Translate between business and technical teams without moving prematurely into solution design.
  • Support testing, requirements validation, defect resolution and implementation activities.
  • Contribute to governance by providing clear, evidence-based analysis to support decisions.
  • Keep analysis focused on business value and the intended outcomes throughout delivery.

What you will bring

You are an experienced Business Analyst who can operate effectively in complex transformation, technology or enterprise systems environments.

More importantly, you know that good Business Analysis is not simply about capturing requirements.

You can listen to what stakeholders are asking for, understand why they are asking for it and determine the underlying need. You are comfortable challenging thinking respectfully, separating facts from assumptions and helping people work through competing priorities.

You will bring:

  • Strong critical thinking and practical problem-solving skills.
  • The confidence to challenge assumptions constructively and respectfully.
  • The ability to distinguish requirements from preferences and proposed solutions.
  • The ability to separate current-state constraints from genuine future-state needs.
  • A clear focus on business value and intended outcomes.
  • End-to-end experience across discovery, process analysis, requirements, testing and implementation support.
  • Strong requirements elicitation, analysis, documentation and validation skills.
  • Experience developing process maps, business rules, user stories and acceptance criteria.
  • Strong workshop facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • The ability to work confidently across business and technology teams.
  • An understanding of how strong requirements support governance and delivery confidence.
  • A pragmatic approach to documentation and governance that supports delivery.
  • Able to start work from October 12th

Highly regarded

Experience in one or more of the following areas will be valuable:

  • Government, local government or broader public sector environments.
  • ERP or enterprise systems transformation.
  • SaaS or cloud-based enterprise platforms.
  • TechnologyOne or OneCouncil.
  • Programs involving multiple workstreams, vendors or delivery partners.
  • Agile, hybrid or traditional delivery environments.
  • Business process optimisation, change impacts and business readiness.

ERP experience is preferred, but it is not essential. Strong Business Analysis experience in comparable transformation environments will also be considered.

Why join this engagement?

You will join an established Davidson Technology Consulting team and provide additional capacity across an active transformation program.

You will work alongside Davidson colleagues and client stakeholders to solve real business problems. Your contribution will help create clearer requirements, improve alignment between business and technology teams, and support informed decisions through delivery.

This is an opportunity for Business Analysts who enjoy getting beneath the initial request, making sense of complexity and helping teams focus on what will deliver genuine business value.

Contract details

  • October 2026 start through to December 2026
  • Brisbane-based with hybrid working - 2 days in office
  • Part of the Davidson Technology Consulting team
  • Additional Business Analysis capacity supporting a complex transformation program

If you are an experienced Business Analyst who thinks critically, asks good questions and is comfortable constructively challenging the status quo, we would like to hear from you.

About Davidson Technology Consulting

Davidson Technology Consulting partners with organisations to shape, deliver and assure technology change, reducing risk and building capability at every scale.

We work alongside our clients to understand the problem, establish a clear path forward and support delivery. Our focus is practical: connecting people, business needs and technology decisions so change can be implemented with greater clarity and confidence.

job.title: Manager Commercial Gas - Territory Generation
job.description:
• Build and lead TGen’s newly established commercial gas function
  • Shape the commercial strategy for a major new gas portfolio
  • Lead complex negotiations, market strategy and commercial growth

Territory Generation (TGen) is the Northern Territory’s trusted energy services business and largest wholesale electricity generator, playing a critical role in powering communities, businesses and industry across the Territory. We own and operate eight power stations, with a diverse generation portfolio spanning gas, diesel, solar, biofuel and battery energy storage.

As the Northern Territory’s energy landscape evolves, TGen is investing in new technologies and energy solutions while maintaining the reliability, affordability and system security essential to the Territory’s future.

Reporting to the General Manager Commercial and Business Development, the Manager Commercial Gas will lead a newly established function responsible for managing and optimising TGen’s gas portfolio across the Northern Territory and East Coast markets. This is a rare opportunity to establish a new commercial capability from the ground up and take strategic responsibility for a significant and complex energy portfolio.

The role will oversee the transition of gas supply and customer contracts into TGen, ensuring reliable supply for the generation fleet while maximising the commercial value of contracted gas. With TGen’s requirements representing only part of the available portfolio, a key focus will be developing and executing the strategies required to optimise surplus gas, manage market exposure and build a sustainable commercial position over the longer term.

You will lead the negotiation and management of complex Gas Supply Agreements, Master Gas Supply Agreements and Gas Transportation Agreements, supported by sophisticated forecasting, pricing, scenario and pipeline analysis. Working across short, medium and long-term market horizons, you will provide strategic advice on portfolio optimisation, gas marketing, risk and emerging opportunities across the NT and East Coast gas markets.

A significant early priority will be establishing the function itself. You will build and lead a specialist team, embed the systems, governance, delegations and risk frameworks required to operate effectively, and establish strong relationships with suppliers, customers, pipeline operators, regulators and government. As the portfolio matures, the focus will increasingly turn to optimising existing arrangements, developing new customer opportunities and positioning TGen to respond to future growth in Territory energy demand.

To be considered, you will bring substantial commercial gas market experience, ideally gained across gas trading, portfolio management, origination, supply or a related commercial environment. You will have demonstrated experience negotiating complex gas supply and transportation agreements, supported by strong capability in financial modelling, valuation, pricing, forecasting and market risk.

Your knowledge of Australian wholesale gas markets and experience dealing with multiple suppliers and customers will enable you to identify value across a complex portfolio. Just as importantly, you will be a credible leader and negotiator, capable of building a high-performing team and navigating relationships across commercial counterparties, regulators, government and senior organisational stakeholders.

This is an opportunity to take ownership of a significant new commercial portfolio and build the capability that will manage it for the future. For an experienced gas commercial leader, it offers a compelling combination of portfolio optimisation, market strategy, complex negotiation and the opportunity to solve a genuine commercial challenge.

job.description:

Complex technology change needs more than a good plan. It needs experienced people who can bring clarity to the challenge, work confidently with senior leaders and stay close to delivery.

We’re looking for a Principal Consultant to join Davidson Technology Consulting in Sydney, with a focus on financial services.

This is a senior, client-facing role with two clear dimensions: leading quality consulting delivery and supporting the development of new client solutions.

You’ll work directly with clients across banking, insurance, wealth, superannuation and related regulated environments. You’ll help them navigate technology transformation, strengthen delivery and make practical decisions with greater confidence.



What you’ll do

You’ll lead and contribute to consulting engagements from problem definition through to delivery.

Depending on the client challenge, your work may include:

  • leading technology transformation and project delivery engagements
  • developing business cases, roadmaps, delivery plans and governance frameworks
  • supporting large-scale transformation programmes across data migration, testing, delivery assurance and programme governance
  • leading transformation design, business analysis, technology delivery, operating model change and implementation readiness

You’ll also help strengthen our relationships across Sydney’s financial services market. Strong delivery comes first. From there, you’ll identify where we can continue helping clients solve real technology and delivery challenges.


What you’ll bring

You’re an experienced consultant who can move comfortably between executive conversations and the detail required to get work delivered.

You’ll bring:

  • 8–10+ years’ experience across consulting, technology delivery, transformation or professional services
  • strong financial services experience, ideally across banking, insurance, wealth, superannuation or another regulated environment
  • established relationships within Sydney’s financial services market
  • experience delivering complex transformation, technology or consulting engagements
  • confidence working directly with senior executives, sponsors and steering committees
  • a track record of producing clear, practical and executive-ready consulting outputs
  • experience contributing to proposals, solution development, statements of work or client presentations
  • strong written and verbal communication skills
  • a practical, outcome-focused approach and a clear commitment to quality.

You won’t need to have delivered every type of engagement listed above. What matters is your ability to understand a complex problem, bring structure to it and help clients move forward with confidence.


Why Davidson Technology Consulting?

For 35 years, Davidson has helped organisations make clearer decisions about their people, capability and future.

Davidson Technology Consulting partners with organisations to shape, deliver and assure technology change, reducing risk and building capability at every scale.

You’ll join a national business with an established client base and collaborative consulting culture. You’ll have the opportunity to work directly with senior financial services leaders, deliver meaningful consulting outcomes and help build our presence in Sydney.

job.title: Head of Safety & Wellbeing - South East Water
job.description:
• Lead the implementation and delivery of South East Water’s strategic safety improvement program.
  • Turn safety ambition into operational reality - strengthen critical controls, lift contractor performance and hold leaders accountable for outcomes.
  • Rebuild the Safety & Wellbeing function and create a culture where safety is owned, not delegate across all levels.

Lead enterprise-wide safety transformation within an essential services organisation.

South East Water is seeking an accomplished safety leader to lead its safety, wellbeing, critical risk, contractor safety, psychosocial risk, injury management and assurance agenda. Reporting to the General Manager People, Safety & Governance, the Head of Safety & Wellbeing will provide strategic leadership across the organisation and work closely with the Board, Executive Leadership Team, senior leaders, employees, contractors, regulators and delivery partners.

The opportunity

The immediate priority of this role is to lead the implementation and delivery of South East Water’s existing strategic safety improvement program. You will translate its objectives into practical operating plans, measurable outcomes and sustainable improvements in leadership accountability, risk ownership and safety performance.

You will also lead the implementation, verification and assurance of effective controls for critical safety risks, ensuring controls are understood, consistently applied and delivering the intended outcomes across operational environments.
A further priority will be strengthening South East Water’s approach to contractor and delivery partner management, including prequalification, onboarding, monitoring, performance management and assurance.

Leading a small team, you will also restructure and uplift the capability, capacity and operating model of the Safety & Wellbeing function to ensure it is aligned to current and future business requirements.

Key responsibilities:

  • Lead the implementation and delivery of the strategic safety improvement program.
  • Strengthen and embed the Safety Management System across all levels of the organisation.
  • Establish visible, felt leadership and clear accountability for safety outcomes.
  • Develop, implement, verify and assure effective controls for critical safety risks.
  • Strengthen contractor and delivery partner safety management.
  • Provide strategic advice to the Executive Leadership Team and prepare high-quality Board and executive reporting.
  • Lead psychosocial risk, wellbeing, injury management and return-to-work strategies.
  • Establish meaningful safety analytics, dashboards, leading indicators and performance reporting.
  • Build leadership capability and foster a culture of learning, risk ownership, accountability and continuous improvement.
  • Maintain and continuously improve the organisation’s ISO 45001-certified Safety Management System.

About you

You will be an experienced and credible safety executive who has led safety, health and wellbeing functions within complex, operationally focused or high-risk environments. You will bring a strong combination of strategic insight, technical expertise, executive presence and the ability to translate safety expectations into practical and sustainable business outcomes.

You will have demonstrated experience in:

  • Leading enterprise-wide safety transformation and cultural change.
  • Delivering safety improvement programs and embedding safety management systems.
  • Developing safety operating plans, governance frameworks, assurance programs and performance measures.
  • Implementing, verifying and assuring critical risk controls.
  • Leading contractor and delivery partner safety across complex operational environments.
  • Managing psychosocial risk, wellbeing, injury management and return-to-work programs.
  • Restructuring and uplifting safety, health and wellbeing functions.
  • Influencing senior leaders and building accountability across complex matrix organisations.
  • Preparing Board and executive reporting for senior stakeholders.

You will hold relevant tertiary qualifications in occupational health and safety, risk management or a related discipline, supported by substantial leadership experience. Experience within water, utilities, infrastructure, construction, energy, transport or another high-risk sector will be highly regarded, particularly where you have led safety transformation, strengthened critical risk controls, improved contractor safety and influenced operational leaders.

Why join South East Water?

This is an opportunity to shape the next phase of safety and wellbeing maturity within an organisation that delivers essential services to the community. You will have the mandate, executive exposure and leadership platform to influence culture, strengthen critical risk management, uplift the Safety & Wellbeing function and create safer, healthier and more resilient outcomes across the enterprise.

For more information on the role, please copy and paste the link to the success profile into your browser: https://tinyurl.com/4msw9tue

For any enquiries or to submit an application for this role, please contact Anthony Grey at Davidson Recruitment on Anthony.Grey@davidsonwp.com or contact 0403 310 566.

JOB TITLE: Senior Auth0 Engineer

  • Configure and manage Auth0 tenants, custom domains, branding and MFA/passkey enrolment flows.
  • Implement and manage Machine-to-Machine (M2M) integrations.
  • Troubleshoot authentication, authorisation and identity integration issues across applications and platforms.

Key Skills & Experience

  • Strong hands-on Auth0 implementation and engineering experience.
  • Strong protocol-level understanding of OAuth 2.0, OIDC and SAML.
  • Experience integrating Auth0 with Java/Spring Boot and .NET applications.
  • Strong understanding of JWTs, refresh tokens, scopes, claims and application authorisation.
  • Experience with Auth0 tenant configuration, custom domains, MFA and passkeys.
  • Experience implementing Machine-to-Machine authentication/integrations.
  • Strong troubleshooting and integration skills across identity and application environments.

job.title: Senior Legal Counsel - NIOA
job.description:
• Senior in-house legal role within a leading Australian defence organisation
  • Advise on complex commercial, government and international contracts
  • Brisbane-based role supporting a growing global business

NIOA is a leading Australian-owned defence company with a growing international footprint and a long history of partnering with government, defence and industry.

An opportunity now exists for an experienced Senior Legal Counsel to join NIOA’s legal team in Brisbane, providing high-quality commercial and legal advice across the NIOA Group.

Reporting to the General Counsel, you will work closely with senior leaders and key stakeholders across the business, providing pragmatic, solutions-focused advice across a broad range of commercial, contractual and regulatory matters.

A significant focus of the role will be drafting, reviewing and negotiating complex commercial agreements, including contracts, subcontracts, deeds, variations and contract change proposals. You will also support negotiations with the Commonwealth, commercial partners and suppliers, including matters involving international and cross-border transactions.

Beyond transactional work, you will help NIOA proactively identify and manage legal risk, interpret legislative and regulatory developments, strengthen contracting frameworks and policies, and contribute to ongoing improvement and innovation across the legal function. As a senior member of the team, you will also have the opportunity to support and mentor more junior legal colleagues.

About You

You will be an experienced commercial lawyer with at least eight years' post-admission experience, ideally combining strong private practice foundations with experience working in-house.

You will bring sophisticated drafting and negotiation capability and demonstrated experience working with complex commercial contracts. Exposure to defence or government contracting, particularly in an international or cross-border environment, will be highly regarded.

Importantly, you will be commercially minded and comfortable operating as a genuine business partner. You can distil complex legal issues into clear, practical and succinct advice, exercise sound judgement under pressure and balance appropriate risk management with the commercial needs of a fast-moving organisation.

You will be proactive, adaptable and highly collaborative, with the confidence to work across different areas of the business while contributing to a small, high-performing legal team.

Candidates must hold a current unrestricted Queensland Practising Certificate and be eligible to obtain and maintain a Baseline Security Clearance.

This is an excellent opportunity for a senior commercial lawyer seeking high-quality, complex legal work in an Australian organisation operating at the intersection of defence, government, manufacturing and international business.

job.title: Change & Knowledge Transfer Manager
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson Technology are working with a leading Federal Government Agency to secure an experienced Change & Knowledge Transfer Manager responsible for assessing, designing and delivering organisational change management and knowledge transfer activities to support the application support and maintenance of the agency’s infrastructure project.


About the Role

You will provide organisational change and knowledge transfer management expertise to strengthen Agency and project capability, effectively managing competing priorities and strategic directions to deliver outcomes aligned with the Agency’s goals and objectives. You will identify, manage and evaluate change and knowledge transfer risks while maintaining a strong understanding of the Agency’s role in delivering digital health outcomes for Australia, its jurisdictional partnerships and key stakeholder relationships. Working within established legislative, policy, project management, change management and governance frameworks, you will operate with a high degree of independence and autonomy under broad direction, resolving complex issues and exercising sound professional judgement in a changing environment. You will make and communicate decisions that may have a significant impact on the Agency and project outcomes, while developing and maintaining strategic relationships and internal and external networks. You will engage and manage a broad range of stakeholders throughout change and knowledge transfer activities, promoting project and Agency objectives while effectively resolving conflict, managing sensitivities and supporting successful outcomes.


About You

You will bring demonstrated experience conducting complex change and knowledge transfer analysis, including assessing impacts, stakeholders and readiness, to develop evidence-based strategies and plans that support successful transition and adoption of new ways of working. You will have experience applying structured change methodologies and leading organisational change activities within transition programs that are already underway, with the ability to operate effectively in ambiguous environments with varying levels of change and knowledge transfer maturity. You will possess excellent organisational, communication and stakeholder management skills, with experience identifying change and knowledge transfer dependencies and collaborating across teams to minimise disruption and operational impact. You will be comfortable navigating complex and sensitive situations and have demonstrated experience planning, coordinating and delivering knowledge transfer between incumbent and incoming vendors to maintain service continuity and minimise operational risk. You will ensure critical business and technical knowledge is effectively shared, documented, recorded and retained in accordance with Agency requirements, and will have experience developing and delivering training materials, user guides, standard operating procedures and support documentation for diverse stakeholder groups. You will also hold tertiary qualifications in Organisational Change Management or a related discipline, or a recognised specialist accreditation such as Prosci.


This role requires Australian Citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a Baseline security clearance (with potential for higher clearance if required) and a national police check.


The Benefits

You will be offered an excellent hourly rate on an initial contract running to the end of the financial year with 2x 12-month extensions available.

job.title: Policy Governance Implementation Lead
job.description:
About the Organisation

Our client is a high-profile, purpose-led organisation operating within a complex and highly regulated environment.

With a strong focus on continuous improvement, innovation and organisational capability, the organisation values different thinking and encourages its people to challenge, improve and evolve how things are done.

This is an opportunity to contribute to a significant organisation-wide initiative with strong executive sponsorship and support.

About the Role

Our client is implementing a centralised, streamlined and fit-for-purpose Policy Governance Framework across the organisation. The framework is already well progressed, and this role will take it from design into practical implementation, adoption and business-as-usual operations.

Working within the Compliance function, you will collaborate across Compliance, Risk, Legal, Technology, project and change teams, partnering with policy owners and subject matter experts to uplift the organisation’s internal corporate policy landscape.

Importantly, this is not a government or public policy development role. The focus is internal corporate policy governance, risk and compliance — establishing consistent standards for how policies are structured, governed, maintained and applied.

You will:

  • Review and uplift existing policies, procedures and supporting instruments against the new framework.
  • Develop practical templates, standards, guidance and resources to support consistent application.
  • Partner with policy owners and SMEs to improve policy quality, consistency and usability.
  • Establish quality assurance processes and provide practical policy governance advice.
  • Support communications, training and change activities to embed the framework into business as usual.
  • Consider how existing technology, including AI, can improve policy development, governance and maintenance.
  • Coordinate multiple stakeholders, priorities and deliverables to maintain momentum and achieve key milestones.

About You

You will bring demonstrated experience implementing a corporate policy governance framework or leading a significant governance uplift within a complex organisation.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have taken a governance framework from design into practical business implementation, rather than those whose experience is primarily policy writing or BAU policy management.

You will ideally bring:

  • Experience across policy governance, framework implementation, risk/compliance and organisational change.
  • Strong experience engaging multiple policy owners and SMEs and influencing without direct authority.
  • Experience developing practical governance tools, including templates, standards, guidance, training and supporting processes.
  • The ability to translate complex governance requirements into clear, usable solutions.
  • Strong stakeholder management, organisational skills and attention to detail.
  • An understanding of how technology and AI can improve policy consistency, governance and efficiency.

Experience within investment management, superannuation, banking, insurance, financial services or another highly regulated environment will be advantageous; however, demonstrated governance implementation capability is more important than a specific industry background.

Formal tertiary qualifications in business, commerce or law are preferred; however, substantial relevant professional experience will also be considered.

The Opportunity

This is a 0.8 FTE engagement, working four days per week, commencing as soon as possible and currently contracted through to 30 June 2027, with potential for the broader program to continue beyond this date.

The indicative daily rate is approximately $620–$700 + superannuation, depending on experience.

You will join a highly collegiate environment and contribute to an initiative with genuine organisational sponsorship, helping establish a policy governance approach that will become embedded into ongoing operations.


Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Chantelle Flood (chantelle.flood@davidsonwp.com) quoting reference JN -092026-44381. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: Configuration Analyst
job.description:
JOB TITLE: Configuration Analyst
JOB LOCATION: Sydney, NSW (Hybrid)
JOB DURATION: 9 months contract (potential extension)

Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced Configuration Analyst to support and enhance Configuration Management Database (CMDB) capabilities within a critical technology environment.

This role will focus on improving CMDB data quality, governance, and remediation, ensuring the CMDB remains a trusted source of truth for technology assets and services. Working closely with technology teams, service owners, asset managers, and IT Operations Management (ITOM) specialists, you will help maintain accurate, complete, and reliable Configuration Item (CI) data within ServiceNow.

This is a hands-on opportunity for a professional with strong Configuration Management expertise, stakeholder engagement skills, and a commitment to operational excellence.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Identify, analyse, and remediate CMDB data accuracy, completeness, and quality issues.
  • Establish and maintain Configuration Item (CI) ownership, governance frameworks, and accountability across technology teams.
  • Define, monitor, and report on CMDB health metrics, KPIs, and performance indicators.
  • Develop dashboards and reports to provide visibility into CMDB health, compliance, and asset management effectiveness.
  • Implement certification and attestation processes to support ongoing CMDB governance and data integrity.
  • Educate stakeholders on Configuration Management best practices, RACI responsibilities, and the importance of maintaining accurate CMDB data.
  • Collaborate with ITOM teams to investigate Discovery-related issues and improve CMDB data quality.
  • Support asset lifecycle management by reinforcing commissioning and decommissioning processes.
  • Ensure compliance with Configuration Management policies, standards, and governance requirements.
  • Identify opportunities to improve processes, controls, and operational outcomes.

Required Skills & Experience:

  • Hands-on experience with ServiceNow CMDB and Configuration Management processes.
  • Strong understanding of ITIL frameworks and Configuration Management principles.
  • Proven experience in CMDB governance, data quality management, and remediation activities.
  • Experience implementing and maintaining governance and compliance controls.
  • Strong stakeholder management, communication, and influencing skills.
  • Experience developing and maintaining reports, dashboards, KPIs, and performance metrics.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and process improvement capabilities.

Desirable Skills & Experience:

  • Experience with ServiceNow ITOM, including Discovery and related capabilities.
  • Knowledge of asset lifecycle management and Service Asset & Configuration Management (SACM).
  • Experience supporting large-scale CMDB transformation or uplift programs.
  • Exposure to governance, risk, and compliance frameworks in enterprise environments.
  • Experience in financial services, payment systems, or other regulated industries.



Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Bidisha Swayamprava on Bidisha.Swayamprava@davidsonwp.com, quoting reference JN -092026-44367. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: HR Advisor | Workforce & People
job.description:
HR Advisor | Workforce & People

Katherine West Health Board | Katherine, NT

$94,907 – $116,569 + 12% super | Salary packaging | Relocation support




Make your next HR role mean something.




Are you an experienced HR Advisor looking for broader exposure, greater autonomy and the opportunity to work somewhere your contribution genuinely matters?




Davidson is proud to partner with Katherine West Health Board (KWHB), an Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisation providing primary healthcare and health-related programs to Aboriginal communities across approximately 162,000km² of the remote Katherine West region.




KWHB has experienced significant organisational growth and is continuing to strengthen its Human Resources function to support its expanding workforce.




We're now seeking an experienced HR Advisor to join the team in Katherine.




Internally titled Workforce Coordinator, this is a broad, hands-on HR advisory role working closely with the Senior Manager Human Resources and supporting managers and employees across the organisation.




If you enjoy variety, like being close to the action and want the opportunity to develop across the breadth of HR rather than being confined to one specialist area, this could be a fantastic next move.




The opportunity

You'll become a trusted member of a growing HR team, providing practical advice and support across the employee lifecycle.




No two days are likely to look exactly the same.




You'll support managers with day-to-day HR matters, prepare employment documentation, oversee workforce compliance, contribute to HR reporting and process improvement, and help ensure employees joining KWHB have a consistent and culturally appropriate experience.




You'll also have exposure to workplace reviews and investigations, workforce planning and broader organisational improvement initiatives.




Your responsibilities will include:

  • Providing practical HR advice and support to managers and employees
  • Interpreting and applying HR policies, procedures, employment legislation and relevant industrial instruments
  • Preparing contracts, variations, secondments and other employment documentation
  • Supporting recruitment, onboarding, induction and offboarding
  • Monitoring licences, registrations, checks, certifications and other workforce compliance requirements
  • Supporting remuneration changes, pay progression, allowances and contractual changes
  • Maintaining accurate employee records and HR information systems
  • Coordinating workforce logistics including travel, accommodation and remote workforce requirements
  • Preparing workforce reporting and identifying trends, risks and opportunities
  • Contributing to HR policy, procedure and process improvement
  • Supporting workplace reviews and investigations as required
  • Contributing to culturally appropriate induction, orientation and workforce development activities.




    The position also provides an opportunity to support and mentor less experienced HR and administrative team members as the function continues to evolve.




    About you

    We're looking for an experienced HR generalist who is comfortable providing practical advice and doesn't need every answer handed to them.




    You don't need to be the finished product or an ER/IR specialist. You do, however, need enough HR experience and judgement to work through an issue, interpret the relevant policy or legislation, provide sensible advice and recognise when something needs to be escalated.




    You'll ideally bring:
  • Experience at HR Advisor, People & Culture Advisor, Senior HR Coordinator or similar level
  • Practical experience providing HR advice and support to managers
  • Sound knowledge of HR policies, procedures and relevant employment legislation
  • Experience across employment documentation and employee lifecycle processes
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Confidence managing multiple priorities and working autonomously
  • Strong administration, systems and attention to detail
  • Sound judgement, discretion and professionalism
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach
  • The ability to build trusted relationships across a diverse and geographically dispersed workforce.




    Experience in health, community services, government, not-for-profit or an Aboriginal Community Controlled Organisation would be highly regarded, but isn't essential.




    A qualification in Human Resources, Business or a related discipline is desirable rather than mandatory, with equivalent relevant experience also considered.




    Working with Katherine West Health Board

    This role is about more than providing HR advice from behind a desk.




    KWHB supports employees across Katherine and remote Aboriginal communities throughout the Katherine West region. You'll work with people from diverse professional, cultural and community backgrounds and will need to approach those relationships with respect, curiosity and cultural humility.




    KWHB is committed to the recruitment, retention and development of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander employees and to creating culturally safe workplaces where people can develop meaningful careers.




    You'll occasionally travel to remote communities by road and/or light aircraft as part of the role.




    What's on offer?
  • $94,907 – $116,569 + 12% super, negotiable based on relevant skills and experience
  • 6 weeks annual leave + 18% leave loading
  • 2 weeks personal leave
  • Annual CPI increases
  • Salary packaging up to $15,900 per FBT year
  • Meal & Entertainment Card up to $2,650
  • Remote Area Benefits
  • Novated leasing
  • Relocation assistance up to $3,000
  • 6–8 weeks accommodation support on relocation
  • Travel allowance for work-related travel

job.title: Auth0 Solution Architect
job.description:
JOB TITLE: Auth0 Solution Architect
JOB LOCATION: Sydney, NSW
JOB DURATION: Till end of April 2027

We are seeking an experienced Auth0 Solution Architect to support an enterprise identity modernisation program. You will be responsible for designing and delivering enterprise-scale Auth0 solutions, onboarding applications to an existing Auth0 platform, and ensuring secure, scalable and consistent authentication and authorisation across the environment.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design enterprise-grade Auth0 solutions, including tenant strategy, connection architecture, custom domains, branding, session management and migration approaches.
  • Onboard web applications to an existing Auth0 platform using OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC) and SAML.
  • Define application integration, user migration and identity modernisation strategies for legacy identity platforms.
  • Configure and enhance Auth0 capabilities including applications, APIs, enterprise connections, Universal Login, MFA, passwordless authentication, machine-to-machine integrations and Auth0 Actions.
  • Develop solution designs covering connection architecture, federation patterns, token design, user journeys and integration approaches.
  • Lead architecture workshops and provide technical governance across delivery teams.
  • Address complex identity scenarios including user lifecycle management, delegated administration, machine-to-machine authentication and application-specific access models.
  • Support integration testing, UAT, cutover planning and production deployment.
  • Troubleshoot authentication-related issues and ensure applications are successfully onboarded into the existing Auth0 environment.
  • Collaborate closely with business, security, application and delivery stakeholders.

Key Skills & Experience:

  • Proven experience as an Auth0 Solution Architect / Identity Architect delivering enterprise-scale Auth0 solutions.
  • Strong hands-on knowledge of OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, federation, MFA and passwordless authentication.
  • Experience integrating applications with Auth0 and working with existing enterprise Auth0 platforms.
  • Strong understanding of identity migration and modernisation from legacy identity platforms.
  • Experience with Auth0 tenant configuration, Universal Login, custom domains, Auth0 Actions, enterprise connections and APIs.
  • Strong solution architecture, technical design and governance capabilities.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills.


Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Bidisha Swayamprava on Bidisha.Swayamprava@davidsonwp.com, quoting reference JN -092026-44369. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: Senior Auth0 Engineer
job.description:
JOB TITLE: Senior Auth0 Engineer
JOB LOCATION: Sydney, NSW
JOB DURATION: Till end of April 2027

We are seeking a Senior Auth0 Engineer to join a technology team delivering identity and access management solutions. This role is ideal for an experienced engineer with strong hands-on expertise in Auth0, OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, token management, and application integrations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Implement and configure Auth0, including Universal Login, custom databases, enterprise connections, Rules and Actions.
  • Work with Auth0 Management API and Authentication APIs to develop and integrate identity solutions.
  • Design and implement authentication and authorisation solutions using OAuth 2.0, OIDC and SAML.
  • Integrate Auth0 with Java/Spring Boot and .NET applications, including use of relevant Auth0 SDKs.
  • Manage JWT validation, refresh token rotation, scopes and claims mapping into application authorisation models.
  • Configure and manage Auth0 tenants, custom domains, branding and MFA/passkey enrolment flows.
  • Implement and manage Machine-to-Machine (M2M) integrations.
  • Troubleshoot authentication, authorisation and identity integration issues across applications and platforms.

Key Skills & Experience

  • Strong hands-on Auth0 implementation and engineering experience.
  • Strong protocol-level understanding of OAuth 2.0, OIDC and SAML.
  • Experience integrating Auth0 with Java/Spring Boot and .NET applications.
  • Strong understanding of JWTs, refresh tokens, scopes, claims and application authorisation.
  • Experience with Auth0 tenant configuration, custom domains, MFA and passkeys.
  • Experience implementing Machine-to-Machine authentication/integrations.
  • Strong troubleshooting and integration skills across identity and application environments.


Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Bidisha Swayamprava on Bidisha.Swayamprava@davidsonwp.com, quoting reference JN -092026-44368. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

  • Shape assets and services and deliver major projects and capital works for a growing regional municipality.
  • Advise the Chief Executive Officer and Councillors on infrastructure, sustainability and community resilience.

Horsham Rural City Council serves a dynamic regional city of approximately 20,000 residents and a broader catchment of more than 60,000 people across the Wimmera. As a proud agricultural and manufacturing centre with deep ties to the grain, pulse and wool industries, Horsham plays a vital role in Australia’s food security and regional economy. job.title: APS6 Senior Procurement Officer
job.description:
Looking for your next opportunity in Commonwealth procurement?

This APS6-level contract offers the chance to work within a centralised procurement function, supporting a dedicated business area across procurement and contract management.

You will work closely with stakeholders to provide practical procurement advice, manage competing priorities and help deliver compliant procurement outcomes.

Davidson Executive & Talent is partnering with a Federal Government agency to recruit an experienced Senior Procurement Officer for this Sydney-based opportunity.


What you’ll be doing

Reporting to an EL1 Procurement Business Partner, you will:

  • manage procurement and contract management activities
  • provide practical procurement advice to internal stakeholders
  • support procurement activities in line with the Commonwealth Procurement Rules
  • review and quality assure RFx and tender documentation
  • review Statements of Requirements, contracts, work orders and Tender Evaluation Plans
  • work with stakeholders to understand their requirements and progress procurement activities
  • support procurement reporting, administration and continuous improvement
  • manage multiple priorities and deadlines with a high degree of autonomy.


What you’ll bring

You will have demonstrated procurement and contract management experience, ideally within the Commonwealth Government or another public sector environment.

You will also bring:

  • experience supporting RFx and tender processes
  • knowledge of Commonwealth or public sector procurement practices
  • strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills
  • the ability to negotiate, influence and provide clear procurement advice
  • strong attention to detail and quality assurance skills
  • the ability to work independently and manage competing priorities.

Experience in IT or digital procurement, BuyICT panels, SAP, Excel or Power BI will be highly regarded.

What you need to know

  • Location: Sydney
  • Rate: $70–$75 per hour + super
  • Level: APS6 equivalent
  • Hours: 37.5 hours per week
  • Contract: Through to October 2027
  • Working arrangements: Flexible working available, subject to agreement
  • Security clearance: Baseline security clearance required

If you have strong procurement experience and are looking for a longer-term Federal Government contract where you can work with stakeholders across varied procurement activities, we would like to hear from you.

job.title: Senior Estimator – Construction & Fitout
job.description:
Senior Estimator – Construction & Fitout

An established and growing construction and trade services business is looking for an experienced Senior Estimator to strengthen its construction and fitout capability.

This is a newly created role driven by growth. You’ll join two talented developing estimators and become the senior technical presence within the team – remaining hands-on with estimating while providing guidance, structure and mentoring.

The opportunity

This isn’t a role where you’ll step away from estimating to purely manage people. You’ll be actively involved in tenders while helping improve the overall quality and sophistication of the estimating function.

You’ll take responsibility for:

  • Leading and preparing construction and fitout estimates and tenders from initial review through to submission
  • Producing accurate cost plans, take-offs, labour and material build-ups and subcontractor pricing
  • Improving the quality of tender submissions, including methodologies, programmes, qualifications and supporting documentation
  • Reviewing commercial risks, scope gaps, assumptions and margin before submission
  • Providing practical guidance and mentoring to two developing estimators
  • Developing and improving estimating software, systems, templates and cost information
  • Working closely with operations to ensure successful tenders transition effectively into project delivery
  • Building strong relationships with subcontractors, suppliers and key internal stakeholders

About you

You’ll be an experienced estimator who has remained close to the construction and fitout market in recent years and still enjoys being hands-on.

Ideally, you’ll bring:

  • Strong recent estimating experience across commercial construction, fitout or refurbishment projects
  • Confidence managing tenders from initial documentation through to final submission
  • Strong understanding of construction costs, subcontractor packages, programmes and commercial risk
  • Experience producing high-quality tender methodologies and documentation
  • The ability to review and improve estimating processes and systems
  • The capability to mentor less experienced estimators without needing to formally “manage” them
  • A calm, considered and collaborative approach

Why consider this opportunity?

You’ll be joining a business with ambitious growth plans at a point where you can have a genuine impact on how the estimating function develops.

Rather than inheriting a rigid corporate structure, you’ll have the opportunity to bring your experience, improve systems and standards, develop two promising estimators and help shape a function that will support the next stage of the organisation’s growth.

Please submit your current resume to apply in Word document format.

job.title: AO5 Advisor - Real-time Network Management
job.description:
AO5 Advisor - Governance, Process & Training Framework

If you are good at turning complex processes into clear guidance that people can actually use, this role offers the chance to make a practical impact across a large operational environment.

Davidson Executive & Talent is partnering with a Queensland Government department to appoint an AO5 Advisor - Governance, Process & Training Framework (Real-time Network Management). This role will support improvements to the department's incident and disruption management processes. You will review existing practices, strengthen governance, develop clear instructions and create training materials that can be used by teams across Queensland.

You do not need to come from a technical or systems operations background. What matters is your ability to understand a process, identify what needs to improve and translate that into practical documentation, governance and training.


What you'll be doing

You will work with operational teams and stakeholders to improve the way processes are documented, communicated and applied.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • reviewing and updating disruption management governance documentation
  • developing governance documentation for planned events
  • reviewing existing processes and identifying opportunities for improvement
  • developing procedures, work instructions and supporting materials
  • creating practical training content for system users
  • coordinating the rollout of training across the state
  • supporting workflow procedures and maintaining accurate documentation
  • uploading and maintaining relevant materials in SharePoint
  • supporting data requests as required
  • working with internal and external stakeholders to ensure information is clear, accurate and fit for purpose.

Intrastate travel may be required to operational facilities.


What you'll bring

You will be comfortable working through detail while keeping sight of how processes affect the people using them.

We are looking for someone who can bring:

  • experience developing training materials, procedures or work instructions
  • an understanding of governance, risk and compliance
  • strong attention to detail and a focus on data and document quality
  • clear written and verbal communication skills
  • strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities
  • confidence working with a range of stakeholders
  • a practical approach to continuous improvement
  • the ability to learn new processes and systems without needing a technical background.

Experience working in government, regulated or operational environments may be useful, but your ability to develop clear governance, documentation and training will be particularly important.


The engagement

The proposed contract runs from 1 October 2026 to 25 June 2027, with the possibility of extension.

The role is up to 38 hours per week, Monday to Friday, with hours worked between 7 am and 6 pm. No resource is required during the shutdown period from 24 December 2026 to 3 January 2027, or on public holidays during the engagement.

If you enjoy bringing structure to complex processes and creating guidance that helps people work with greater clarity and consistency, we would like to hear from you.



Apply NOW to be considered for this opportunity.

job.title: Manager, Water and Waste
job.description:
Lead essential services. Shape critical infrastructure. Make an impact you can see.

There are leadership roles where you maintain what already exists. Then there are opportunities to shape what comes next.

Davidson Executive & Talent is partnering with Cook Shire Council to appoint its next Manager Water and Waste, leading the essential water, wastewater and waste services that support communities across one of Queensland’s most unique regions.

Based in Cooktown and reporting to the Director Infrastructure, you’ll lead an experienced team of approximately 28 people across water, wastewater, waste and electrical maintenance. You’ll also oversee an operating budget of approximately $9.3 million across these essential services.

Your remit combines technical leadership with asset management, commercial thinking, regulatory compliance and long-term service planning.

The opportunity
This is a role for a leader who wants to build, improve and influence.

There is a significant infrastructure agenda ahead, including new and upgraded water and wastewater infrastructure in Lakeland and Coen, alongside the opportunity to strengthen asset management and shape a practical future waste strategy.

Your early priorities will be clear:

  • Strengthen regulatory and legislative compliance
  • Improve asset management and long-term infrastructure planning
  • Lead, mentor and get the best from an experienced, long-tenured team
  • Build robust business cases that connect infrastructure needs with funding and investment decisions
  • Bring a commercial lens to operational and capital planning
  • Manage and optimise a significant operating budget across water, wastewater and waste services
  • Work confidently with executives, councillors, regulators, contractors and communities

The role spans a large geographic footprint, so visible leadership matters. You’ll spend time with your people, understand the assets firsthand and be comfortable getting out across the region rather than leading solely from behind a desk.

The leader we’re looking for
Your strongest technical grounding will be in water and wastewater. You understand treatment, infrastructure, compliance and the consequences of getting essential services wrong.

You’ll also bring:

  • Leadership experience across water, wastewater and/or waste services
  • Strong asset lifecycle, renewal and capital planning capability
  • Commercial and financial acumen, including responsibility for significant operating budgets and business cases
  • Sound knowledge of relevant regulatory and environmental requirements
  • Experience leading people through change and improving established ways of working
  • The ability to turn complex technical issues into clear recommendations and gain stakeholder support
  • Strong judgement, communication and stakeholder management skills
  • Relevant engineering qualifications or extensive equivalent experience

You don’t necessarily need to come directly from local government. If you bring the technical credibility, commercial judgement and leadership capability, Council can support you in understanding its processes and environment.

Why Cooktown?
Cooktown may not have been where you expected your next career move to take you. That could be exactly what makes this opportunity worth exploring.

You’ll be joining a close-knit organisation with people who care deeply about their community. Council’s Director Infrastructure describes the management team as among the best they have worked with across their career in Australia and internationally, highlighting its integrity, low-ego approach and genuine commitment to community outcomes.

Cooktown offers a very different pace to metropolitan life, without being disconnected from the essentials. The region has schools, health services and airport access, with Cairns approximately a 45-minute flight away. Housing can be challenging, and Council can assist successful candidates in navigating local accommodation options.

We’ll be open about the move, the location and what the role involves. We want you to understand Cooktown properly and decide whether the opportunity is right for you.

Ready for something different?
If you’re an experienced water and wastewater leader looking for greater scope, visible impact and the opportunity to help shape essential infrastructure for the future, we’d like to start a conversation.

You don’t need to have made your mind up about Cooktown before you call.


For a confidential discussion, contact William Stock at Davidson Executive & Talent on william.stock@davidsonwp.com

job.title: Culture and Capability Manager
job.description:
Davidson is proud to partner with Anglican Church Southern Queensland (ACSQ) in the appointment of a newly created Culture & Capability Manager.

ACSQ is one of 23 Dioceses that form the Anglican Church of Australia. Through its network of parishes, schools, education and care services, community services, ministry education and social justice and advocacy, ACSQ plays an important role in communities across Southern Queensland.

Following a recent organisational culture review, ACSQ is investing in its People & Culture capability and creating this role to help translate the findings and commitments from that review into meaningful and sustainable change.

The opportunity

Reporting to the Group Manager, People & Culture, the Culture & Capability Manager will take ownership of developing and delivering ACSQ's culture and capability agenda.

This is a role for someone who enjoys taking an organisation from insight to action.

You will work closely with senior leaders to understand the organisation, its people and its culture, before translating priorities into a practical roadmap that can be delivered and measured.

Your remit will span culture, organisational development, leadership capability, learning and development, employee engagement and change. You will design and facilitate workshops, develop capability initiatives and annual learning programs, strengthen organisational values and support leaders to create a more connected and leader-led culture.

Communication will also be an important part of the role. You will help create greater visibility around the culture and capability agenda, ensuring employees understand what is changing, why it matters and the progress being made.

Working closely with the People Operations Manager, you will help ensure that improvements to culture and capability are supported by strong People & Culture foundations and contemporary ways of working.

What you will bring

We are looking for an experienced Culture, Capability, Organisational Development or senior People & Culture professional who can operate strategically while remaining highly focused on delivery.

You may have developed culture strategies before, but more importantly, you will be able to demonstrate how you have turned those strategies into action and delivered tangible outcomes.

You will ideally bring:

  • Strong experience across organisational development, culture and capability
  • A solid broader Human Resources / People & Culture foundation
  • Experience designing and delivering organisation-wide culture or change initiatives
  • Leadership and manager capability development experience
  • Strong facilitation skills and confidence leading workshops with varied stakeholder groups
  • Experience developing learning, development and capability frameworks
  • The ability to translate employee feedback and organisational insights into practical priorities and actions
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage employees around change
  • Experience partnering with executives and senior leaders and influencing decisions
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to build credibility quickly
  • The judgement and political awareness to navigate sensitive organisational issues appropriately
  • Resilience, pragmatism and a genuine bias for action
  • The ability to work independently and achieve outcomes within a relatively lean environment
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications or equivalent professional experience

What is important is an ability to work respectfully within the values and ethos of the Anglican Church and to understand the nuances of a complex, purpose-led organisation.

The person

This role will suit someone who is credible, practical and action oriented.

You will need to be comfortable entering an organisation where there is a genuine appetite for change, but also recognise that sustainable culture change takes time.

You will be able to listen carefully, understand different perspectives and build trust, while still maintaining momentum and appropriately challenging the organisation when decisions need to be made.

Above all, ACSQ is looking for someone who can get things done someone who can develop the framework, bring people with them and then ensure the commitments made translate into visible action.




Why join ACSQ?

This is a rare opportunity to step into a newly created position with the ability to genuinely shape the organisation's future culture and capability.

You will have visibility and support from senior leadership and the opportunity to establish a function and framework that has not previously existed in this form.

Success will mean employees can see and feel the progress being made – through stronger leadership, clearer communication, improved capability and a more connected organisational culture.

The role offers $180,000 + super, with a Brisbane CBD location and some flexibility to work from home. Given the stakeholder and relationship-building requirements of the role, there will be an expectation to spend the majority of the initial period in the office.

If you are an experienced culture and capability professional who enjoys moving beyond strategy into delivery and wants the opportunity to make a meaningful organisational impact, we would love to hear from you.

job.title: Data Engineer
job.description:
About Barwon Water

Davidson has partnered with Barwon Water to appoint experienced Data Engineers to join its Digital Engineering team and help strengthen the organisation’s enterprise data capability required to support one of regional Victoria’s most significant transformation agendas.

Barwon Water delivers water, sewerage and recycled water services to more than 330,000 people across the Geelong region and surrounding communities. Through a major Digital Business Transformation program, the organisation is investing in new technologies, operating models and ways of working that will shape the future of the business and the communities it serves.

About the Role

  • Design, build and operate scalable batch and near-real-time data pipelines, models and reusable data products that support trusted analytics, reporting and approved AI use cases.
  • Build and maintain data solutions across Microsoft Fabric, including Lakehouses, Warehouses, PySpark notebooks and Data Factory pipelines, transforming enterprise data into trusted datasets and semantic models.
  • Engineer data quality into solutions through validation, profiling, reconciliation and monitoring, ensuring issues are identified and managed before they impact downstream users.
  • Apply modern engineering practices including Git-based source control, automated testing, deployment automation, peer review, monitoring, alerting and production support to deliver reliable and maintainable solutions.

About You

  • Strong hands-on data engineering experience across Microsoft Fabric or comparable modern data platforms such as Azure Databricks, Synapse or Snowflake, with experience building layered Lakehouse architectures, data models and pipelines.
  • Strong SQL and working Python skills, with experience ingesting data from SaaS platforms, cloud services and on-premises enterprise systems using secure and supportable integration patterns.
  • Experience building reliable data pipelines with data quality controls, error handling, monitoring and safe rerun processes, along with the ability to troubleshoot and contribute to root cause analysis in production.
  • A strong technical mindset combined with commercial awareness and a consulting approach, with the ability to explain technical trade-offs to business stakeholders, collaborate with engineers and work effectively within Agile delivery teams.

The Benefits

This is a unique opportunity to contribute to Barwon Water’s growing enterprise data capability during a significant digital transformation. You’ll design scalable data pipelines, models and products that enable trusted analytics, reporting and AI outcomes, while working alongside a collaborative Digital Engineering team committed to innovation and continuous improvement.

Based in Geelong, this permanent full-time role offers a hybrid working model with three days per week in the office, providing flexibility while supporting close collaboration with stakeholders and delivery teams.


Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Adnan​ Haidermota on adnan.haidermota@davidsonwp.com, quoting reference JN -092026-44228. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: Senior Program Manager – Projects & PMO
job.description:
Senior Program Manager – Projects & PMO

Davidson is partnering with a growing Australian organisation operating across resource recovery, telecommunications, infrastructure and Defence-related environments to appoint a Senior Program Manager – Projects & PMO.

Reporting to the General Manager, you will lead the national delivery and governance of a diverse project portfolio while developing the organisation’s PMO capability.

This is a senior, hands-on project leadership role focused on creating consistency, strengthening governance and ensuring projects are delivered safely, commercially and in line with contractual, regulatory and customer requirements.

The opportunity

You will take ownership of project performance across a national portfolio, with responsibility for:

  • Providing national oversight across Resource Recovery, telecommunications, infrastructure and Defence-related projects
  • Establishing and developing PMO governance, reporting, systems, templates and delivery standards
  • Leading, coaching and supporting Project Managers and project teams
  • Directly managing high-value, complex or strategically significant projects
  • Monitoring project budgets, forecasts, margins, variations and financial performance
  • Maintaining strong risk, issue, change and escalation processes
  • Ensuring Defence-related projects meet relevant security, contractual, HSEQ and compliance requirements
  • Building strong relationships with clients, executives, operational leaders, contractors and external stakeholders
  • Coordinating project resourcing and workforce capability across multiple locations
  • Driving continuous improvement across project delivery, reporting, governance and operational performance

About you

You will bring significant project management experience delivering complex, multi-site or national projects.

Your background could come from telecommunications, infrastructure, Defence, resource recovery or another complex field-based project environment.

The priority is finding an accomplished project leader with strong capability across:

  • Project governance – risk management, change control, reporting and delivery assurance
  • Commercial performance – budgeting, forecasting, cost control, variations and margin management
  • PMO development – establishing or improving project systems, standards and governance frameworks
  • Leadership – coaching Project Managers, setting clear expectations and building accountability
  • Stakeholder management – confidently engaging with senior executives, clients, contractors and operational teams
  • Compliance – strong understanding of WHS/HSEQ, contractor management and operational requirements

You will also be comfortable managing multiple concurrent projects and competing priorities across different locations, with strong digital literacy across Microsoft Office/Excel and operational or compliance platforms.

The ability to meet any relevant security clearance or Defence-related requirements will also be important.

Leadership with purpose

The organisation combines strong commercial performance with a clear social purpose, creating meaningful employment and development opportunities for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.

You will bring a leadership style that balances commercial accountability, strong governance and delivery discipline with coaching, inclusion and people development.

Experience working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people would be valued but is not essential. Alignment with the organisation’s purpose and a willingness to undertake cultural competency training are important.

The opportunity to grow

This role offers the opportunity to shape how projects are delivered nationally, strengthen PMO capability and establish the systems and governance needed to support continued growth.

It could suit an established senior project leader looking for broader portfolio responsibility, or an experienced Program or Project Manager ready to step into a role with greater national leadership and strategic influence.

You will have the opportunity to lead complex and strategically important projects while helping build a more consistent, scalable and commercially disciplined project delivery function.

job.title: National Operations Manager - Resource Recovery
job.description:
Melbourne preferred | Brisbane considered | National remit

Lead national operations. Build consistency. Unlock value from every asset.

Davidson is partnering with a growing Australian organisation operating across resource recovery, recycling and secure asset processing to appoint a National Operations Manager – Resource Recovery.

Reporting to the General Manager and leading approximately 3–4 Site Managers, you will oversee a growing network of processing facilities across Australia.

This is a hands-on leadership role focused on making the national operation work efficiently, consistently and commercially – ensuring valuable assets and recovered materials are accurately tracked, effectively processed and moved through the right channels.

The opportunity

You will take ownership of operational performance across multiple sites, with responsibility for:

  • Leading and developing Site Managers across the national network
  • Establishing consistent operational processes, controls and performance standards
  • Managing the receipt, tracking, processing, storage and movement of assets and recovered materials
  • Maintaining strong inventory reconciliation, asset tracking and chain-of-custody controls
  • Overseeing logistics and material movements between customers, facilities and downstream processors
  • Driving productivity, labour efficiency, safety, cost and margin performance
  • Maximising the recoverable value of processed materials and commodities
  • Monitoring processing volumes, inventory movements and operational KPIs
  • Supporting the establishment and mobilisation of new sites as the network expands
  • Driving continuous improvement across systems, processes and operating models
  • Maintaining strong safety, environmental and regulatory standards

About you

Your background could come from e-waste, metals recycling, resource recovery, secure asset recovery, reverse logistics, waste management, industrial processing, warehousing or logistics.

Direct recycling experience would be advantageous, but the priority is finding an accomplished operational leader with strong capability across:

  • Logistics – transport, material movements, warehousing, scheduling and multi-site coordination
  • Inventory control – reconciliation, stocktakes, shrinkage, chain of custody, asset tracking and audit
  • Operations leadership – leading multiple sites and developing operational managers
  • Commercial performance – improving productivity, labour utilisation, costs and margins
  • Systems and process improvement – experience with ERP, WMS, inventory or production systems

Exposure to commodity pricing, recovered-material sales or downstream processors would be beneficial but isn't essential.

Leadership with purpose

The organisation combines commercial and environmental performance with a strong social purpose, creating meaningful employment and development opportunities for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.

You will bring a leadership style that combines clear commercial accountability with coaching, inclusion and people development.

Experience working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people would be valued but isn't essential. Alignment with the organisation's purpose and a willingness to undertake cultural competency training are important.

The opportunity to grow

This could suit an established national leader or an ambitious Regional or State Operations Manager ready to step into their first national role.

You will have the opportunity to shape a growing national operation, develop its people and establish the systems and processes required to support its next phase of growth.

Please submit your current resume to apply. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com
