job.title: People Operations Manager
job.description:
Davidson is proud to partner with Anglican Church Southern Queensland (ACSQ) in the appointment of a newly created People Operations Manager.

ACSQ is one of 23 Dioceses that form the Anglican Church of Australia. Through its network of parishes, schools, education and care services, community services, ministry education and social justice and advocacy, ACSQ plays an important role in communities across Southern Queensland.

Following a recent review of the People & Culture function, ACSQ is investing in its capability and creating this role to provide experienced operational leadership across People & Culture.

The opportunity

Reporting to the Group Manager, People & Culture, the People Operations Manager will take ownership of day-to-day People & Culture operations, providing practical and trusted advice to leaders and managers while strengthening the processes, systems and governance that support the employee lifecycle.

This is a hands-on senior HR role. You will work across a diverse stakeholder environment, partnering with senior leaders, managers, clergy and employees to navigate people matters, build manager capability and create a more consistent and contemporary People & Culture service.

A key focus will be supporting a shift towards a leader-led, People & Culture-enabled model building the confidence and capability of managers to take greater ownership of their people, while ensuring they have the right frameworks, advice and support around them.

You will also have the opportunity to identify what can be done differently and better. From improving workflows and reducing manual processes through to strengthening governance, policies, employee records and service delivery, you will play an important role in building the foundations for the future People & Culture function.

What you will bring

We are looking for an experienced People & Culture professional who has operated at this level before and understands what good looks like.

You will bring strong generalist HR capability and demonstrated experience across employee and workplace relations, organisational change, performance, manager coaching and the broader employee lifecycle.

Importantly, you will be someone who can build trusted relationships while still being prepared to provide clear advice and appropriately challenge established ways of working.

You will ideally demonstrate:

  • Significant senior generalist HR experience within a complex organisation
  • Strong employee and workplace relations capability, including the management of complex and sensitive matters
  • Sound knowledge of the Fair Work Act, modern awards and contemporary employment practices
  • Experience improving HR processes, systems, governance and ways of working
  • The ability to coach and influence leaders while strengthening manager accountability
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills across a diverse organisation
  • Experience working through organisational change or transformation
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach and the ability to turn ideas into action
  • Strong judgement, resilience and the ability to navigate complexity and competing priorities
  • A relevant tertiary qualification in Human Resources, Industrial Relations, Business or a related discipline is desirable

What is important is an ability to work respectfully within the values and ethos of the Anglican Church and an appreciation of the unique environment in which ACSQ operates.

Why join ACSQ?

This is an opportunity to join the organisation at an important point in the evolution of its People & Culture function.

You will work closely with an experienced leadership team, have genuine scope to influence how People & Culture services are delivered and help establish stronger foundations that will support the organisation for years to come.

The role offers $180,000 + super, with a Brisbane CBD location and some flexibility to work from home. Given the relationship-focused nature of the position, there will be an expectation to spend the majority of the initial period in the office and engaging with stakeholders across the Diocese.

If you are an experienced People & Culture leader who enjoys getting close to the business, improving how things work and building trusted relationships, we would love to hear from you.

To apply, Please apply with current resume in Microsoft Word format only (.doc or .docx). If you would like to have a confidential discussion, please contact Catherine Lyttle. Want to know more about Davidson? Visit us at www.davidsonwp.com

job.title: Account Manager - Emerging Accounts
job.description:
About Davidson

Davidson brings together expertise across people, strategy, and technology to help organisations perform at their best. Founded in 1991, we listen closely, understand the challenge and apply practical, experience-led thinking helping organisations move forward with confidence. Our focus is on bringing clarity to complexity and supporting stronger, more resilient futures.

Within Davidson Technology Consulting, we partner with organisations to shape, deliver, and assure technology change, reducing risk and building capability at every scale.

About the Role

Davidson Technology Consulting is growing, and we’re looking for an Account Manager - Emerging Accounts to play a key role in what comes next. You’ll build on Davidson’s existing relationships to expand our Technology Consulting presence across our client network and develop selected new accounts.

You’ll open broader technology conversations, build connections with senior decision makers and identify where our capability can address their needs. Working with Senior Partners and delivery teams, you’ll turn opportunities into stronger client partnerships and sustainable commercial growth.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Grow emerging Technology Consulting accounts across Davidson’s client network, expanding relationships and identifying new areas of opportunity.
  • Open new doors within existing clients, building relationships with senior technology, digital and business decision makers.
  • Create, convert, and grow opportunities to advise, augment capability, or deliver technology outcomes.
  • Develop account growth plans identifying priority stakeholders, opportunities, and clear actions to increase our presence.
  • Build and convert a strong pipeline against commercial targets, with disciplined forecasting, and clear next steps.
  • Turn client and market insight into growth, bringing Davidson relationships and expertise together to develop commercially sound opportunities in priority markets.

What We're Looking For

You’ll have experience growing accounts within consulting, professional services or solution sales. You’ll bring:

  • A track record of growing accounts, creating opportunities, and delivering revenue outcomes.
  • Strong business development capability, with the ability to open new relationships and expand existing ones.
  • Confidence engaging senior and executive stakeholders and turning conversations into opportunities.
  • Commercial judgement and negotiation skills to progress and convert opportunities.
  • An understanding of technology change and how to connect client challenges with relevant solutions.
  • Financial services or complex enterprise experience and established industry networks would be valuable.

Why Join Davidson

At Davidson, you will be part of a business growing and evolving with the challenges our clients face. We bring together expertise across people, strategy, and technology, giving you the opportunity to help grow our Technology Consulting business, work alongside capable people and build your career in a business focused on what comes next.

Access to experienced leaders: Work closely with senior leaders and decision makers, with the autonomy to contribute ideas and make an impact.

Flexibility that supports good work: Work in a flexible, hybrid environment designed to support performance and wellbeing.

Recognition for the contribution you make: Be part of a culture recognising individual and team effort, contribution and results.

Ready to step into your next chapter?

If you enjoy growing relationships, opening new conversations, and turning client needs into practical technology opportunities, we’d like to hear from you.

job.title: APS6 Senior Performance and Evaluation Officer
job.description:
Turn evidence into insight and help demonstrate the impact of significant national programs.

This is a role for someone who wants performance and evaluation work to influence real decisions.

Davidson is seeking an experienced Senior Performance & Evaluation Officer to join a major Australian Government program focused on sustainable agriculture, natural resource management and environmental outcomes.

You’ll work across a large-scale national portfolio of 178 projects, backed by significant government investment and focused on improving productivity, building resilience and increasing natural capital.


Why this role?

You won’t simply collect data and produce reports.

You’ll work with teams across the organisation to strengthen how performance is measured, evaluated and communicated. You’ll turn complex program information into clear evidence that supports policy, program and operational decisions.

For someone with strong monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL), performance reporting or program management experience, it’s an opportunity to work at scale and see your insights contribute to nationally significant programs.


What you’ll be doing

You’ll take a lead role across performance reporting and evaluation, including:

  • managing corporate and program performance reporting
  • strengthening monitoring, evaluation, learning and reporting approaches
  • analysing performance information to identify insights and lessons
  • developing evidence-based advice for program and policy decision-making
  • contributing to program reviews, evaluations and learning initiatives
  • identifying opportunities to improve performance and evaluation practices
  • developing practical MEL tools and guidance
  • preparing clear briefs, reports, talking points and presentations
  • building productive relationships across internal and external stakeholder groups
  • potentially supervising a small team of up to three people.


What will help you succeed

You’ll be someone who can take complex information and make it useful.

You’ll bring experience in program management, program performance reporting and/or monitoring, evaluation and learning, supported by strong analytical thinking and sound judgement.

You’ll also be able to demonstrate:

  • experience leading or supervising a small team
  • the ability to work with limited direction and manage competing priorities
  • strong conceptual, analytical and problem-solving skills
  • confidence working collaboratively across multiple teams
  • strong stakeholder engagement skills
  • excellent written communication, with the ability to write clearly for different audiences
  • professionalism, accountability and a focus on continuous improvement.

Practical experience applying MEL concepts and tools will be particularly valuable. Experience in natural resource management or sustainable agriculture is well regarded, but it isn’t essential.


The opportunity at a glance

Contract: 12 months, with potential extension of up to 10 months
Rate: $70–$80 per hour + super
Hours: 37.5 hours per week
Location: Australia-wide
Flexibility: Partial work from home or flexible arrangements may be negotiated
Travel: Occasional regional and remote travel may be required
Clearance: Baseline security clearance required
Proposed start: 12 October 2026


Interested?

If you’re experienced in performance, evaluation or program management and want your work to help shape better decisions and demonstrate meaningful program impact, we’d like to hear from you.

Apply now or contact Natalee Thorpe on Natalee.Thorpe@Davidsonwp.com at Davidson for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Training Lead - SAP
job.description:
JOB TITLE: Training Lead
JOB LOCATION: Brisbane, QLD
JOB DURATION: 12 – months contract (potential extension or conversion)

Project Context

The public sector client is undertaking a major ERP transformation, migrating a customised SAP ECC6 environment to SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud. The program follows SAP Activate methodology, delivered across multiple horizons and waves, and spans core functions including Finance, Asset Management, Maintenance, Procurement, Payroll and more. Alongside the technical migration, the organisation is using the transformation to rationalise enterprise structures and move toward a "clean core" SAP model. Capgemini is engaged as the Business Transformation/Solution Adoption Partner, supporting the design, build and adoption of the new solution across the organisation.

Role Purpose

The Training Lead is accountable for the successful delivery of the Learning & Capability workstream within Solution Adoption, ensuring the workforce is trained, capable and ready to operate SAP S/4HANA and the associated business process changes. The role leads training strategy, learning needs analysis, curriculum design, content development, delivery and capability uplift throughout the SAP Activate lifecycle, working closely with the Change Lead to ensure learning and change activities are fully integrated.

Key Responsibilities:

Training Leadership & Delivery

  • Lead the end-to-end delivery of the Learning & Capability workstream across all horizons and waves.
  • Develop and execute the Training Strategy, Training Plan and supporting learning materials.
  • Ensure training activities are integrated with solution design, testing, deployment and transition to BAU.

Learning Needs Analysis & Curriculum Design

  • Lead Learning Needs Analysis in parallel with Fit-to-Standard workshops across impacted business functions.
  • Design persona-based, role-specific learning pathways aligned to new SAP S/4HANA processes, responsibilities and system interactions, covering distinct workforce segments such as leadership and executives, people leaders, operational leaders, enabling function users, frontline/technical personnel, administration users and light users.
  • Prioritise and sequence learning content against confirmed business need, addressing both new functionality and refresher training for existing processes requiring capability uplift, rather than developing content generically.
  • Translate Change Impact Assessment outputs and solution design decisions into targeted learning interventions.

Training Content Development & Delivery

  • Lead the development of training materials, facilitator guides, digital learning assets, simulations, job aids and evaluation tools, developed through SAP WalkMe as the primary learning content platform.
  • Design and deliver end-user training and Train-the-Trainer activities during Deploy, using blended modalities suited to a distributed, shift-based and operational workforce.
  • Coordinate training environments, test scripts and scenario-based exercises with functional and technical SAP teams to ensure content reflects the configured solution.

Train-the-Trainer & Capability Uplift

  • Establish and lead the Super User and Trainer network, providing advanced system knowledge and facilitation skills to support peer coaching and local adoption reinforcement.
  • Build sustainable internal capability and support capacity during deployment and beyond go-live, in collaboration with the Change Management team.
  • Deliver refresher training and post-go-live capability reinforcement during Run/Hypercare, supporting transition to business-as-usual ownership.

Governance, RAID & Reporting

  • Own training-related RAID items alongside the project analyst and Business Readiness & Adoption Analyst, including identification, management and escalation of training risks, issues, assumptions and dependencies.
  • Report training completion and competency rates through LMS reporting, attendance records, assessment results, knowledge checks and learner evaluations, feeding into overall business readiness and go-live decision-making.
  • Maintain the Training Needs Analysis and role-based Learning Pathway templates and other governance artefacts, and support training-related governance forums.

Digital Enablement & Insights

  • Oversee the deployment and use of SAP WalkMe, and any complementary digital adoption tooling, to support training delivery and adoption measurement.
  • Leverage training completion data and analytics to identify remaining capability gaps, engagement trends and readiness risks, feeding program-level readiness and adoption dashboards.
  • Provide evidence-based recommendations on training effectiveness and capability uplift to program leadership.

Key Outcomes

  • A workforce trained and capable of operating SAP S/4HANA and new business processes at go-live, with refresher capability uplifted on existing processes.
  • Persona-based training pathway coverage across all impacted functions, waves and workforce segments, including frontline and operational users.
  • Training completion and competency rates tracked and reported against agreed go-live thresholds.
  • Effective integration of training with change, communications and readiness activities across the SAP Activate lifecycle.
  • Sustainable internal capability through Train-the-Trainer and Super User networks.
  • Successful transition to business-as-usual operations and long-term capability ownership.

Experience & Capability

  • Extensive experience leading training or learning workstreams for large-scale ERP and SAP transformations; SAP S/4HANA experience is highly regarded.
  • Demonstrated expertise in Learning Needs Analysis, persona-based curriculum design and training delivery across large, complex, multi-site organisations, including frontline/operational workforces.
  • Hands-on experience developing and governing learning content in SAP WalkMe, and working knowledge of Learning Management Systems for completion tracking and reporting.
  • Experience designing and leading Train-the-Trainer and Super User enablement programs.
  • Strong facilitation, workshop leadership and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Experience working within multi-vendor environments in collaboration with System Integrators, PMOs and business stakeholders.
  • Ability to lead and develop a small training analyst team, and to work collaboratively with the Change Lead to ensure integrated adoption outcomes.



Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Bidisha Swayamprava on Bidisha.Swayamprava@davidsonwp.com, quoting reference JN -092026-44340. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: Power Platform Developer
job.description:
About the Company

Our client is an Australian enterprise operating within the infrastructure industry.

About the Role

This role focuses on designing and delivering secure, scalable, and well‑governed solutions using the Microsoft Power Platform to support business productivity and digital transformation initiatives.

You’ll work closely with business stakeholders, architects, and platform governance teams to translate requirements into fit‑for‑purpose applications and automation solutions that deliver real business value.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design, build, and maintain enterprise solutions using Microsoft Power Platform, including Power Apps (Canvas & Model‑Driven), Power Automate, Dataverse, and Power Pages
  • Develop workflows, integrations, and automation solutions to improve operational efficiency and data quality
  • Extend low‑code solutions with pro‑code where required (e.g. Power Fx, JavaScript, Azure Functions, Logic Apps, Microsoft Graph APIs)

job.title: Senior Systems Engineer
job.description:
About the Company

Iberdrola Australia is leading Australia’s transition to a clean energy future. With over 170 years history, the Iberdrola Group today is a global energy leader. Their expertise includes renewable energy, networks, smart grids, large-scale energy storage, energy innovation and digitisation, and advanced customer products.

Their generation portfolio is more than 95% renewable and includes 9 wind farms, 3 solar farms, 2 grid scale batteries and 2 fast-start peakers and continuing to evolve, investing in new capabilities in networks and offshore wind. Iberdrola’s financial strength, supply chain access and history of award-winning expertise, will make Iberdrola a certain partner to accelerate Australia’s Net Zero emissions future.

Iberdrola is now recruiting for a Senior Systems Engineer to work on the new VNI West project based in the Melbourne CBD office.

This is an opportunity to shape your career with one of the genuine global energy leaders within Australia.

About the Role

The Senior Systems Engineer (Systems Engineering and Assurance) will implement and maintain the project Systems Engineering framework, ensuring that stakeholder, regulatory, contractual and technical requirements are captured, managed, allocated, verified and validated throughout the project lifecycle.

The role provides leadership across requirements management, assurance, verification and validation, interface management and systems integration. It ensures alignment with the Systems Engineering Management Plan (SEMP), Systems Engineering Management Framework (SEMF), project governance requirements and applicable international Systems Engineering standards.

The position acts as custodian of requirements traceability and assurance evidence within the Requirements Management System, preferably Relatics, supporting design development, delivery, testing, commissioning and handover.

Some specific responsibilities include:

· Lead the implementation and application of Systems Engineering processes in accordance with ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 and the project Systems Engineering Management Plan (SEMP).

· Establish, manage and maintain project requirements, including baselines, allocation, traceability, configuration control and change management within Relatics or the approved Requirements Management System.

· Facilitate requirements elicitation, analysis and stakeholder engagement activities to ensure requirements are clear, measurable, verifiable and aligned with project objectives.

· Develop and maintain end-to-end requirements traceability between stakeholder needs, design deliverables, verification activities, assurance evidence and project outcomes.

· Coordinate Contractors, Engineering Designers and Owner’s Engineers to ensure consistent application of Systems Engineering and Systems Assurance approaches across the supply chain.

· Support the development and maintenance of system architectures, system breakdown structures, operational concepts, interfaces and other Systems Engineering artefacts.

· Implement and support Systems Assurance activities, including assurance reviews, governance forums, compliance assessments and stage gate approvals.

· Develop and coordinate verification and validation strategies, plans, matrices and activities to demonstrate compliance with project requirements and operational needs.

· Identify, manage and coordinate system interfaces across project disciplines, contractors, stakeholders, regulators and external parties, ensuring interface risks and actions are effectively managed.

· Administer and optimise Relatics, including workflow configuration, reporting, dashboards, data governance, user support and assurance performance metrics.

· Deliver Relatics training and Relatics configuration development for wider Project Management.

· Assess and manage Systems Engineering, assurance, interface and configuration risks arising from design, requirements and project changes, ensuring impacts are understood and controlled.


About You

To be successful in this role you will have tertiary electrical engineering qualifications and strong experience in a similar role within energy or renewables (preferred) or other large, complex capital infrastructure (rail, defence, utilities). Training and certification with INCOSE will be well regarded.

Your excellent interpersonal skills allow you to build effective working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders, resulting in exceptional performance.

You will be able to work in a very hands-on, flexible and practical manner while thinking strategically, and you will be comfortable and able to travel interstate to both office and site locations when required.

The Benefits

This is an exceptional career opportunity to join a world leader in renewable energy and work on a nationally significant transmission line project.

  • Review status and health indicators to ensure they accurately reflect underlying delivery performance.
  • Identify and log data conflicts between source registers for management review.
  • Maintain a data quality tracker documenting fields, sources, issues and remediation status.
  • Prepare a concise handover briefing outlining residual gaps, assumptions and outstanding matters.

Key deliverables:

  • Master initiative crosswalk.
  • Individual-level initiative baseline template for all active initiatives.
  • Re-linked master schedule with dependency integrity checked.
  • Data quality tracker and reconciliation log.
  • Handover briefing note summarising residual gaps and assumptions.

About You

  • Demonstrated experience integrating and reconciling data from multiple, inconsistent source systems.
  • Strong Excel skills, including formulas, pivot tables and data validation.
  • Experience using Power Query, or an equivalent tool, to merge and manage large datasets.
  • Working knowledge of project and portfolio management artefacts, including schedules, RAID logs, benefits registers and baselines.

The Benefits

job.title: A07 Health and Wellbeing Principal Advisor
job.description:
About the Company

Our client is a large and complex organisation delivering civil construction and maintenance services across Queensland. With approximately 1,300 employees, supported by significant labour hire and subcontractor workforces, the organisation operates across a diverse range of environments throughout the state.

With a strong focus on worker health and safety, the organisation is continuing to strengthen its approach to health, wellbeing and workplace risk management.


About the Role

This is an opportunity for an experienced health and wellbeing professional to lead and continuously improve enterprise-wide programs that protect worker health and support a safe, healthy and productive workforce.

This is a senior specialist technical and advisory position with no direct reports. Success will be driven by your subject matter expertise, professional judgement, stakeholder engagement and ability to influence outcomes across the organisation.

Working closely with operational leaders, health and safety professionals, occupational hygiene specialists and external service providers, you will provide specialist leadership and advice across worker health, fitness for work, psychosocial wellbeing and hazardous exposures.

  • Leading health monitoring and health surveillance programs, including governance, implementation, oversight and contractor management
  • Supporting fitness for work programs encompassing fatigue, drug and alcohol management and related assurance activities
  • Leading psychosocial risk management and worker wellbeing initiatives
  • Managing health risks associated with hazardous exposures including lead, respirable crystalline silica, asbestos, noise and chemicals
  • Supporting exposure monitoring programs and associated health-related training
  • Developing and reviewing policies, standards, procedures, guidance materials and governance frameworks
  • Identifying and implementing practical, enterprise-wide solutions to health and wellbeing challenges
  • Providing trusted specialist advice to operational and corporate stakeholders.


About You

You are an experienced health and wellbeing professional who can operate independently, navigate complex issues and translate technical requirements into practical operational outcomes.

You will bring strong professional judgement and the confidence to influence stakeholders without direct authority. Comfortable taking ownership of complex challenges, you can work through technical, operational and stakeholder considerations to deliver effective solutions with minimal supervision.

  • More than five years’ experience across health, occupational hygiene, workplace wellbeing, health and safety or a closely related discipline
  • Demonstrated experience managing legislated health monitoring and health surveillance programs
  • Strong experience implementing fitness for work programs, including fatigue and drug and alcohol management
  • Experience leading psychosocial risk management and workplace wellbeing initiatives
  • Experience developing enterprise-level frameworks, systems, standards, procedures and improvement programs
  • Experience managing health risks associated with hazardous substances and exposures
  • Experience within civil construction, construction, transport, infrastructure, utilities, resources, rail or another comparable high-risk industry
  • The ability to build strong relationships and translate specialist technical requirements into practical business outcomes.


The Benefits

This is an opportunity to step into a senior specialist position offering broad organisational influence and genuine enterprise-wide scope.

Rather than leading through people management, you will lead through expertise, influence and trusted advice. You will have the autonomy to take complex programs from concept through to implementation and play an important role in strengthening worker health and wellbeing outcomes.

You will also have access to occupational hygiene and specialist technical support when required, while taking ownership of governance, programs and practical improvement initiatives across the organisation.

For an experienced practitioner who enjoys solving complex problems, influencing organisational change and delivering meaningful worker health outcomes, this is an opportunity to make an impact across a substantial and diverse operational workforce.

Vendor, commercial and stakeholder management

job.title: Market Analyst
job.description:
Davidson is the proud recruitment partner of SEC Victoria as they accelerate Victoria’s renewable energy transition.

Do work that makes a difference

SEC is building an enterprising and dynamic team to accelerate Victoria’s transition to renewables and help achieve Victoria’s renewable energy target of 95% by 2035. We are working together for renewable, affordable, reliable energy for all Victorians.

Your role
As a Market Analyst in the Energy Markets Analytics team, you will deliver insights that inform critical long-term decisions across the organisation. With PLEXOS modelling at the core of the role, you will analyse Australian energy market trends, interpret complex modelling outputs, and provide strategic recommendations to support key business initiatives. You will also contribute to the development of analytical tools and systems that drive data-informed decision-making.

You will bring strong hands-on PLEXOS experience, ideally in short-term price forecasting, with the ability to translate modelling outcomes into actionable insights. Supported by programming skills in Python, R, or SQL, and proficiency in Excel, Power BI, or Tableau, you will combine technical expertise with strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills to deliver value in a fast-paced and collaborative environment.

This role can be based in either our Melbourne CBD office or our regional office located in Morwell.

What you will do:
Core accountabilities include:

  • Modelling & forecasting: Enhance SEC’s market modelling capabilities, including short-term probabilistic forecasts, long-term capacity expansion, and dispatch optimisation models. Improve integration, quality, and usability of outputs to support strategic decision-making.
  • Scenario analysis: Contribute to developing energy transition scenarios by applying market expertise and judgement, and support documentation of assumptions and scenarios for stakeholder and Board endorsement.
  • Project due diligence: Partner with internal teams and external advisors to assess prospective investments and support asset and contract valuations, contributing to analysis and reporting.
  • Data management & visualisation: Improve the collection, organisation, analysis, and visualisation of market data from sources such as AEMO, ASX Energy Futures, and SEC systems.

Who you are:
Experiences and Skills:

Must Have:

Your capabilities and areas of expertise that matter most for this role are:

  • Hands-on experience with PLEXOS, ideally including short-term schedule price forecasting;
  • Proficiency in programming languages to support data processing and workflow development, with preferences for Python, R and/or SQL;
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to collaboratively interpret data and modelling outputs and produce and distribute meaningful insights across the organisation;
  • Numerical and computing skills to support the development of accessible analytical and reporting tools including Advanced Excel, PowerBI, and/or Tableau;

Highly Desirable:

  • Demonstrated knowledge and experience in the Australian energy market, particularly regarding the operation of wholesale markets, renewable energy assets, financial markets, and trading systems;
  • Tertiary qualifications (honours or advanced desirable) in Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Economics, Finance and/or another relevant specialisation;
  • An appreciation of Victorian Government policy targets, initiatives, and goals.

An empowered workforce
A career with SEC means you’ll be joining a new and vibrant ‘for purpose’ government-owned renewable energy company that:

  • Empowers you to influence how we accelerate Victoria’s renewable energy transition and decarbonise our economy.
  • Inspires you through meaningful, challenging work in an environment that encourages leadership and an entrepreneurial spirit.
  • Supports your growth through career advancement and professional development opportunities.
  • Provides hybrid work arrangements, with around 3 days working in Melbourne or Morwell, with flexible work options to meet individual circumstances, providing greater choice and autonomy.

How to Apply
We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. We are also deeply committed to building an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and people with disability, people from the LGBTIQ community, and people from culturally diverse backgrounds. SEC strives to create a respectful and collaborative workplace culture that allows all employees to thrive.

For further information and to explore this opportunity further please contact SECRecruitment@davidsonwp.com

Please click the ‘Apply Now’ button. As part of the application process, you will need to provide a copy of your resume and/ or a cover letter (optional) addressing how your skills, knowledge and experience will be relevant to this role. Note: Applicants must be an Australian citizen, permanent resident or hold a valid work permit to be eligible to apply.





Please apply with current resume in Microsoft Word format only (.doc or .docx). If you would like to have a confidential discussion, please contact Rodney Roberts on 03 9929 9500, quoting reference JN -062026-43647. Want to know more about Davidson? Visit us at www.davidsonwp.com

job.title: Manager AI, Data and Intelligence
job.description:
Manager AI, Data and Intelligence | Gippsland Water

About Gippsland Water

Davidson has partnered with Gippsland Water to appoint a Manager AI, Data and Intelligence, a senior leadership opportunity responsible for shaping the organisation’s enterprise approach to artificial intelligence, data and analytics, innovation, enterprise architecture and business improvement.

Gippsland Water provides essential water and wastewater services across the Gippsland region, supporting its customers, communities and the long-term prosperity of the region. Operating within a highly regulated environment, the organisation is focused on using technology, data and innovation responsibly to improve customer outcomes, organisational performance and sustainable value.

About the Role

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer and leading a small team, the Manager AI, Data and Intelligence will bring together AI, data and analytics, innovation, enterprise architecture, process improvement and efficiency as an integrated enterprise capability.

You’ll lead the development of strategies, governance frameworks, roadmaps and standards that enable Gippsland Water to adopt AI and emerging technologies responsibly, strengthen the quality and accessibility of enterprise data and translate new ideas into practical and measurable business outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the development and evolution of enterprise strategies and roadmaps across AI, data and analytics, innovation, enterprise architecture and business improvement.
  • Establish and mature AI and data governance frameworks, ensuring responsible use across privacy, cyber security, ethics, risk and regulatory requirements.
  • Lead the enterprise approach to data management, business intelligence and analytics, improving data quality, accessibility and confidence in organisational information.
  • Shape enterprise architecture principles, capability maps, target-state views and transformation roadmaps that connect business strategy with technology investment.
  • Lead innovation initiatives, AI pilots and proofs of concept from opportunity identification through to scaled delivery and business-as-usual adoption.
  • Establish business cases and benefits realisation frameworks that demonstrate the value, productivity improvements and return on investment generated through AI and technology initiatives.

About You

You’re an experienced transformation, technology or data leader who knows how to turn emerging technologies into meaningful business outcomes. You can see the bigger picture, but you’re equally comfortable getting into the detail required to move ideas from strategy through to execution.

You’ll bring experience across AI, data governance and enterprise transformation, with the ability to establish practical frameworks, prioritise opportunities and manage the risks associated with emerging technology. You’ll be confident engaging with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, translating complexity into clear direction and building organisational capability along the way.

Must-Haves

  • Substantial experience across strategy, transformation, technology, innovation, business architecture, business improvement or organisational capability roles.
  • Demonstrated experience across AI and data governance, data quality and risk, ideally within a regulated or complex environment.
  • Strong experience across AI and data governance, data quality and risk, ideally within a regulated or complex environment.
  • Experience developing and implementing governance frameworks, policies, standards or operating models.
  • Proven ability to take AI, data and technology opportunities from strategic thinking through to practical execution and measurable business outcomes.

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience leading enterprise-wide change, innovation or capability development within a regulated or complex organisation.

Benefits & Why Gippsland Water

This is a unique opportunity to take on a highly influential leadership position at the intersection of AI, data, innovation and enterprise transformation, with genuine exposure to executive leadership, the Board and stakeholders across Gippsland Water.

Based in Traralgon, this is a permanent full-time position offering a flexible working model, a competitive salary package and additional benefits. You’ll have the opportunity to shape how Gippsland Water responsibly adopts AI and emerging technologies while building the data, governance and enterprise capabilities required to deliver sustainable value for customers, communities and the wider Gippsland region.

Apply Now

To be considered for this opportunity, click Apply Now or contact Cameron Smith via email (Cameron.smith@davidsonwp.com) for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Project Director – Hong Kong – International Contractor
job.description:

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Lead and develop a multidisciplinary project team, creating a collaborative and performance-focused project environment.
  • Maintain a clear focus on successful project outcomes across construction, programme, commercial performance, safety and quality.
  • Work closely with senior construction, commercial, design and engineering leaders to identify priorities and maintain momentum across the project.
  • Build productive relationships with the client, joint venture partners, consultants and key project stakeholders.
  • Provide senior-level oversight of project performance, identifying emerging challenges and ensuring appropriate actions are taken.
  • Navigate complex project interfaces and competing priorities while maintaining alignment across the broader delivery team.
  • Provide leadership through critical phases of construction, commissioning and project completion.
  • Promote effective communication and collaboration across a diverse, multicultural project environment.
  • Foster a strong culture of accountability, safety, quality and continuous improvement.
  • Represent the project at senior stakeholder and leadership forums and provide clear reporting on overall project performance.

About You

We are seeking an established construction leader who has developed their career through the delivery of significant and complex building projects.

You are likely to have:

  • Extensive experience within the major building and construction sector, supported by relevant tertiary qualifications.
  • A successful track record in senior project leadership roles with responsibility for complex, high-value developments.
  • Experience taking projects through challenging delivery phases and maintaining performance in demanding construction environments.
  • The ability to lead and influence large teams comprising construction, engineering, design, commercial and project management professionals.
  • A strong understanding of the commercial and contractual considerations associated with major construction projects.
  • The confidence and credibility to engage with clients, project partners and senior stakeholders at an executive level.

Of greater importance is a demonstrated track record leading the delivery of major, technically complex building projects.

The Opportunity

This is a significant senior leadership opportunity with an established international contractor delivering a major development in Hong Kong.

With a substantial pipeline of major building and infrastructure investment across the region, the position also provides longer-term opportunities for an experienced construction leader looking to build their career within the Asian market.

Candidates currently working with mid-tier or top-tier contractors will be considered, with the emphasis on major project delivery experience, leadership capability, commercial acumen and the ability to successfully operate within a complex project environment.

For further information or a confidential discussion regarding the opportunity, please contact Neil McEwan on 0403 597 905.

job.title: Project Manager / Business Analyst
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson Technology are working with a State Government Department to secure an experienced Project manager / Business Analyst to work within the Privileged Access Management team.


About the Role

As the Project Manager / Business Analyst, you will lead the day-to-day coordination and business analysis activities for the production implementation of Keeper Privileged Access Management (PAM). You will be responsible for establishing and maintaining the integrated project plan, schedule, budget, governance, procurement activities, risks, issues and dependencies, while coordinating delivery across multiple specialist technology and cyber security teams. Alongside your project management responsibilities, you will gather and document business, technical, security and operational requirements, develop process flows and acceptance criteria, and ensure requirements remain traceable to agreed project outcomes. You will drive stakeholder actions and decisions, coordinate testing, defect resolution, assurance and reporting, and manage readiness for the production pilot. A key focus will be bringing the various technical workstreams together without taking over their platform accountability, ensuring training, communications, operational documentation, support arrangements and knowledge transfer are completed so the Keeper PAM solution can be successfully accepted and transitioned into BAU.


About You

To be successful, you will bring a minimum of seven years’ experience delivering projects within large-scale ICT environments, with demonstrated success managing complex infrastructure, identity, cyber security or enterprise platform implementations through to production and operational acceptance. You will combine strong project management capability across planning, scheduling, budgets, procurement, governance, RAID, dependencies and executive reporting with hands-on business analysis experience encompassing requirements elicitation, process mapping, acceptance criteria, traceability, testing support and operational readiness. You will have experience coordinating multidisciplinary technical teams and vendors, ideally across cyber security, Privileged Access Management (PAM), Identity and Access Management (IAM) or Essential Eight initiatives, and a sound understanding of enterprise technologies including Linux, Windows Server, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, MFA, networking and high-availability environments. You will be confident navigating organisational financial, procurement, security and change controls, coordinating vendor delivery and licensing, and producing concise, evidence-based executive, assurance, milestone and financial reporting. Your ability to build strong relationships and translate effectively between business, operational, security and highly technical stakeholders will enable you to drive actions and decisions through to closure, while your experience coordinating production implementation, testing, change, training, knowledge transfer and BAU handover will ensure solutions are successfully transitioned into operation. Relevant project management and business analysis certifications are highly regarded, while previous experience with Keeper PAM or another privileged access management platform will be advantageous.


The Benefits

You will be offered a 6-month contract on an excellent hourly rate and the ability to negotiate a flexible working arrangement for the duration of the assignment.


Please submit your current resume to apply. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: SAP Solution Architect
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson Technology are working with a large State Government Department to secure Solution Architect is to provide expert advice and content knowledge in regard to the continual provision of leadership on architecture and related initiatives.


About the Role

As the Solution Architect, you will provide architectural leadership and expert advice across the design, development, integration and ongoing enhancement of enterprise solutions, ensuring technology outcomes align with business requirements and organisational strategy. You will analyse business requirements and system specifications, develop solution architecture and detailed design documentation, and ensure solutions comply with relevant technical strategies, standards, policies, governance and cyber security requirements. You will lead the identification and resolution of complex architectural and technology challenges, manage solution risks and issues, and assess proposed changes to ensure designs remain robust, scalable and fit for purpose. You will work closely with business owners, technical teams, project teams, vendors and other stakeholders to define and deliver agreed outcomes, while providing expert advice and quality assurance across key project deliverables. You will maintain contemporary knowledge of enterprise and postmodern ERP solutions, preferably SAP, and apply emerging technologies and architectural practices where appropriate. You will also support effective knowledge transfer, solution handover and capability uplift to ensure Queensland Health teams are equipped to support and enhance solutions following implementation.


About You

To be successful in this role, you’ll be an experienced Solution Architect with extensive expertise designing and delivering complex SAP solutions within highly integrated, large-scale ERP transformation environments, including demonstrated experience within Queensland Government. You will bring strong knowledge across SAP finance and supply chain domains, including General Ledger, Asset Accounting, Accounts Payable and Receivable, Management Accounting and Budgeting, Asset Management, Real Estate, Inventory Management, Operational Procurement and Extended Warehouse Management. You will have significant architectural experience developing integration strategies, solution architectures and Solution Integration Designs, with the ability to translate complex SAP technical concepts into practical solutions that achieve business outcomes. You will be experienced in developing and presenting high-quality architectural and solution artefacts and working across multiple technical and business teams to maintain an integrated end-to-end solution. You will demonstrate strong leadership capability, including coaching and mentoring architects, leading team members and supporting the delivery of high-quality services within agreed deadlines and service levels. Your highly developed communication, consultation and negotiation skills will enable you to provide strategic advice, influence complex decisions and build effective relationships with senior stakeholders and clients in changing environments. You will also maintain contemporary knowledge of ERP and integration technologies, industry trends, systems integration and service-oriented architecture, with experience across Health or similarly complex enterprise environments highly regarded.


The Benefits

You will be offered a contract through to 30th June 2027 with possible extension, on an excellent daily rate and the ability to negotiate a flexible working arrangement for the duration of the assignment.


Please submit your current resume to apply. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: Network Design Engineer
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson have partnered with a global technology and data leader powering the live environment; think major venues, elite sport and entertainment. With teams across APAC, the US and EMEA, you’ll help deliver strategy-through-to-operations solutions that make big moments unforgettable.


About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Network Design Engineer / Consultant to design the critical network infrastructure behind some of Australia’s most exciting stadiums, arenas, major events and complex infrastructure environments.

Working within the client's multidisciplinary design team, you’ll translate operational, user and technical requirements into secure, resilient and scalable network solutions. You’ll take ownership of defined work packages across the full project lifecycle - from early concepts and detailed design through procurement, construction, commissioning and operational readiness.

This is an opportunity to combine hands-on network engineering with client-facing consulting, contributing to sophisticated environments where performance, reliability and event-day readiness are essential.

The role may be based in Melbourne, Sydney or Brisbane, with some project-related travel required.

About You

You’re an experienced network engineer who enjoys turning complex requirements into practical, well-coordinated solutions. You’re confident managing your own deliverables, working directly with clients and collaborating across technical and design disciplines.

You bring strong engineering judgement, attention to detail and the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

You’ll Bring

  • At least five years’ experience in network design, engineering or technology consulting, with increasing responsibility.
  • Strong knowledge of enterprise routing, switching, wireless networking, IP addressing, VLANs, redundancy, QoS, multicast, monitoring and network security.
  • Demonstrated experience producing network designs, technical specifications, schematics, schedules and reports across multiple project stages.
  • Experience working on complex venues, buildings, campuses, transport, infrastructure or similarly integrated technology projects.
  • A relevant tertiary qualification in engineering, information technology, telecommunications or a related discipline, or equivalent industry experience.
  • Strong written, verbal and visual communication skills, with confidence contributing to client workshops and design meetings.
  • Australian working rights and the flexibility to attend project sites and travel when required.

Professional-level certifications such as Cisco CCNP, Aruba ACSP/ACMP or Juniper JNCIP would be highly regarded. Experience with high-density Wi-Fi, network access control, software-defined networking, cloud-managed networks or converged technologies such as AV-over-IP, IPTV, broadcast and electronic security would also be valuable.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop LAN, WAN, WLAN and data centre or communications-room architectures across concept, schematic and detailed design stages.
  • Prepare logical and physical network designs covering topology, redundancy, routing and switching, addressing, segmentation, security, QoS and network management.
  • Design networks supporting converged services such as corporate ICT, building systems, AV-over-IP, IPTV, broadcast, security, ticketing, point-of-sale, voice and venue operations.
  • Produce technical specifications, network schematics, connectivity diagrams, rack elevations, equipment schedules, bandwidth assessments and design reports.
  • Coordinate network requirements with structured cabling, wireless, cybersecurity, audiovisual, security, broadcast, electrical and architectural disciplines.
  • Evaluate vendor solutions and recommend fit-for-purpose technologies based on interoperability, lifecycle, supportability, sustainability and whole-of-life value.
  • Facilitate requirements workshops and design meetings with clients, venue operators, consultants, contractors and technology vendors.
  • Review tenders, contractor proposals, shop drawings, product submissions and technical departures against the approved design intent.
  • Respond to technical queries during construction and undertake site inspections, testing, commissioning and operational-readiness activities.
  • Manage assigned work packages to agreed quality, programme and budget expectations.
  • Contribute to technical standards, design tools, peer reviews and the development of graduate and junior engineers.

job.title: Payroll Officer

job.title: Recruitment Consultant
job.description:
You’ve learned how to recruit. You know how to build a market, develop relationships, win work and deliver results.

But maybe you’ve started wondering whether there should be more to this career than the next vacancy, placement and fee.

We think there should be.

Recruitment is where the conversation starts.


At Davidson, a vacancy might simply mean a client needs a great person. That’s our bread and butter and something we’re proud to do well.

But sometimes there’s a bigger problem.

Why can’t they attract the people they need? Why are good people leaving? Is it capability, culture, process, structure or technology?

Being part of a broader Davidson business spanning Executive & Talent, Strategy & Performance and Technology Consulting means you can ask better questions, bring other expertise into the conversation and build deeper client relationships.

We’re a large, privately owned Australian business with more than 35 years behind us.

We have scale, but we don’t want bureaucracy. Our consultants build markets, create industry events, develop communities and bring new ideas into the business.

  • You’ll get plenty of autonomy here. But autonomy comes with accountability.
  • We have KPIs. We have targets. We expect you to work hard, win business and deliver.
  • We just don’t believe good recruiters need to be told exactly how to do it.

Davidson isn’t for every recruiter.

If you need someone structuring your day, you may find the freedom uncomfortable.

If you don’t like change, you’ll probably find us frustrating.

And if you’re a great individual performer but your success comes at the expense of the team, this definitely isn’t the place.

We like high achievers. We just like humble ones.

We work hard. We challenge each other. We celebrate together. And when things get tough, we look after each other.


Davidson is entering its next chapter, and there’s plenty still to build.

So we’re looking for experienced recruiters who don’t necessarily want to leave recruitment. They just want to see how much further they can take it.

If that sounds like you, contact us, ask us the difficult questions.

Decide for yourself whether Davidson could be right for you.


Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Michael Donnelly at michael.donnelly@davidsonwp.com, quoting reference JN -092026-44257. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

The role will work closely with Site Managers, Owner’s Representatives, and O&M contractors to ensure that safety processes meet Iberdrola’s obligations and standards for safe and sustainable operations.

Some specific responsibilities include:

· Implement and coordinate the Health and Safety Assurance Program across operational sites and business activities.

· Plan, schedule and conduct assurance activities, including inspections, audits, verifications, workplace observations and critical control effectiveness reviews.

· Support the implementation of the Enterprise Critical Control Program and verify the effectiveness of critical controls through assurance activities.

· Undertake first- and second-line assurance activities in accordance with organisational assurance requirements.

· Monitor compliance with Health and Safety Management System requirements, corporate standards, legal obligations and regulatory requirements.

· Support operational leaders and contractors to understand and meet health and safety assurance requirements.

· Participate in incident investigations and verify the implementation and closure of corrective and preventive actions.

· Support the development and implementation of corrective action plans arising from audits, investigations, inspections and assurance reviews.

· Support organisational learning through the facilitation of lessons learned reviews, post-incident reviews and knowledge-sharing activities.

· Provide coaching and practical guidance to leaders and workers on assurance processes, risk management and critical control verification.

· Participate in contractor prequalification, mobilisation and contractor assurance activities to verify compliance with contractual and legislative requirements.

· Support the preparation of management review reports, assurance summaries and performance dashboards.

About You

To be successful in this role you will have relevant qualifications and strong experience in health, safety and environment in large, complex renewable energy, construction, mining, oil and gas or similar industry. Additional qualifications in auditing, assurance, incident investigation and risk management will also be highly regarded.

Your excellent interpersonal skills allow you to build effective working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders, resulting in exceptional performance.

You will be able to work in a very hands-on, flexible and practical manner while thinking strategically, and you will be comfortable and able to travel interstate to both office and site locations when required.

An open, unrestricted drivers’ licence is required.

The Benefits

This is an exceptional career opportunity to join a world leader in renewable energy and work on a wide variety of projects alongside a globally experienced team.

job.title: Head of Operations
job.description:
Lead the operation. Build the capability. Help shape the next phase of growth.

Davidson is partnering with an established Queensland multi-trades business to appoint a Head of Operations during an exciting period of growth and transformation.

With more than 70 years of history, the organisation has developed a strong reputation across plumbing, electrical, roofing, building and general trade services. Building upon an established maintenance business, it is now expanding its construction and fit-out capability and investing in the leadership, systems and operational structure required to scale successfully.

Reporting to the executive leadership team, the Head of Operations will lead operational delivery across all trade divisions. This is a broad leadership position combining people management, project and service delivery, commercial performance, client relationships and continuous improvement.

You will inherit a capable workforce and a supportive, family-oriented culture. Your challenge will be to build upon these foundations, introducing greater structure, accountability and consistency while protecting the values that have contributed to the organisation’s success.

The opportunity

You will:

  • Lead operations across maintenance, construction and fit-out activities.
  • Provide leadership to Heads of Department, Account Managers, operational teams and site-based employees.
  • Build the operational capability required to support significant business growth.
  • Improve workforce planning, scheduling, productivity and utilisation across multiple trades and projects.
  • Monitor labour, materials, costs and job margins to improve commercial performance.
  • Introduce meaningful KPIs and establish clear accountability across the operation.
  • Improve systems, processes, policies and reporting, including the effective use of Simpro.
  • Oversee a blended workforce of permanent employees, subcontractors and outsourced personnel.
  • Maintain strong relationships with existing clients while supporting new business and service opportunities.
  • Champion a strong safety culture and ensure compliance with relevant legislation, standards and company procedures.
  • Develop leaders, mentor employees and create an environment where people are empowered to perform at their best.

About you

You are an accomplished operational leader with experience in a multi-trade services, building services, facilities maintenance or commercial construction environment.

You will ideally bring:

  • Senior operational leadership experience within a complex, labour-intensive business.
  • An understanding of both recurring maintenance services and construction or fit-out projects.
  • Experience leading trade-based workforces, subcontractors and multiple operational teams.
  • Strong commercial acumen, including job costing, margin management and resource utilisation.
  • The ability to introduce structure and accountability within a growing, entrepreneurial organisation.
  • Experience improving operational systems, workflows and management reporting.
  • Strong knowledge of safety, quality and compliance requirements.
  • A practical, visible and approachable leadership style.
  • The confidence to challenge constructively, make decisions and follow through.
  • Strong client relationship and stakeholder management capabilities.

A trade, construction or relevant technical background would be valuable, although your leadership capability, commercial judgement and experience scaling operations will be most important.

The opportunity to make an impact

This is an opportunity to join an established Queensland business at a pivotal stage in its development. You will have the autonomy and executive support to influence how the organisation operates, develops its people and builds the platform for its next phase of growth.

The organisation offers the stability and reputation of a long-standing business, combined with the energy, ambition and opportunity of a company preparing to grow rapidly.

job.title: Project Manager – Telecommunications / Resource Recovery
job.description:
Project Manager – Telecommunications / Resource Recovery

Permanent Full Time | Hybrid

  • Lead and grow national telecommunications resource recovery programs
  • Own project performance across delivery, budgets, compliance and stakeholders
  • Combine strong commercial outcomes with meaningful social impact

About the Company

Our client is an established Australian technology decommissioning and resource recovery organisation with a strong focus on sustainability and social impact.

Operating as a certified Social & Indigenous Enterprise, the organisation combines commercial performance with a commitment to creating employment pathways and opportunities for Indigenous Australians. It has received significant industry recognition for its work across sustainability, supplier diversity and Indigenous social enterprise.

The business is experiencing significant growth, nearly doubling its workforce over the past two years. Its Resource Recovery operations have also expanded considerably, with teams now delivering programs across multiple Australian states.

About the Role

Reporting to the Head of Resource Recovery, the Project Manager will take ownership of the operational delivery and continuous improvement of national telecommunications Resource Recovery programs.

You will manage programs including copper cable and exchange hardware removal and disposal, ensuring projects are delivered safely, on time and within budget while meeting environmental, social, governance and Indigenous employment objectives.

This is a hands-on position within a fast-paced and growing operation. You will play an important role in supporting continued expansion while maintaining strong commercial outcomes across the broader program.

Working closely with internal leaders, field teams, contractors and major telecommunications clients, you will lead geographically dispersed teams, manage budgets and forecasts, oversee contractor and asset compliance, maintain strong HSEQ standards, manage risks and escalations, and develop effective processes to support consistent delivery.

About You

You will be an experienced Project Manager who is comfortable operating autonomously and taking ownership in an environment where priorities move quickly.

Ideally, you will bring approximately 4–5 years of project management experience, with telecommunications or infrastructure experience highly regarded. Most importantly, you will have demonstrated experience delivering commercially successful projects and understand how to balance profitability with broader organisational and social objectives.

You will bring strong financial management capability across budgeting, forecasting and reporting, together with proven leadership experience and the ability to build and grow teams. Strong stakeholder management, knowledge of WHS/HSEQ and contractor compliance, and confident decision-making will also be important.

You are a self-starter who is prepared to get hands-on, solve problems and establish priorities independently. Telecommunications experience is desirable, while candidates from closely aligned infrastructure environments will also be considered.

The Benefits

This is an opportunity to join a rapidly growing organisation and take ownership of a significant, expanding national program.

You will have genuine influence over project and team performance, the opportunity to help build and develop growing operations, and exposure to established long-term telecommunications programs.

Importantly, this role offers something beyond traditional project delivery: the opportunity to achieve strong commercial outcomes while contributing to employment pathways and positive social impact for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities.
